**2026-08-30 — Land Placement Slice 3 built (`docs/land-placement-slice3-brief.md`): the fence writer, `create_land` skeletons, `ShapeGroup` expansion, the `reExpand()` merge rule, the remaining offset kinds and frames, and P2-P5 as pure predicates. No panel, no canvas, no importer — those stay slice 4/5 by the brief's own scope.**

All seven items landed, each ending green on its own test file under `src/tools/builtin/landPlacement/`.

**1. `fence.ts` (Sec.6.1).** Locates the two markers (`/* @alp v1 begin … */`, `/* @alp end */`) as a plain nesting-depth walk over `commentOpen`/`commentClose` token KINDS — deliberately not alias-aware, since this module only has to find fences it wrote itself, and its own escaping (next paragraph) guarantees one it wrote can never trigger alias-based nesting. `readFenceModel` returns null on any of the three malformed shapes the brief names (truncated JSON, wrong `v`, no `@alp-model` key at all) — never repairs, never partial-adopts. `buildFenceEdits` regenerates wholesale and returns `[]` when the candidate text is byte-identical to what's already there (idempotence), or appends a fresh fence at end-of-file when none exists (a placeholder insertion point; slice 4's panel owns a real one).

**The hazard the brief flagged (Sec.3, hazard 2) is real and closed by one mechanical fact rather than by hunting for specific dangerous words.** `JSON.stringify` with no indent argument never emits whitespace of its own — every space in its compact output originates from a string VALUE, because JSON's punctuation carries none. So replacing every character in `src/parser/lexer.ts`'s own `WHITESPACE` set (space, tab, `\n`, `\v`, `\f`, `\r` — nothing Unicode) with its `\uXXXX` escape, across the WHOLE compact blob, collapses the entire `@alp-model` payload into one un-splittable lexer token no matter what a user types into a `Placement.label`. `JSON.parse` reads either form identically, so this costs nothing on read. Proven rather than argued: `fence.test.ts` builds a real `commentOpenAliases` set for `SHORE_FISH` (constId 69) via `validate.ts`'s own `commentOpenAliases()`, embeds a label `"a SHORE_FISH ring"` two ways, and shows the NAIVE embed swallows a following `#const AFTER_FENCE 1` as comment trivia (the control — the hazard is real) while the escaped embed leaves it untouched and round-trips the label exactly.

**2. `roleEmit.ts` + `landCommand.ts` (Sec.6.2).** `emitRole` turns a `LandRole`'s four attributes into `#const`s — `terrain` (a `Ref`) rendered directly since it's always one token, `baseSize`/`baseElevation`/`landPercent` (`Expr`) through the ordinary compiler backend so a role attribute that needs hoisting gets it for free. A `fixed` `ZonePolicy` gets its own role constant; `perRepeat` and `none` do not, per Sec.6.2's one named exception. `buildCreateLandSkeleton` writes every attribute as a reference except the two per-repeat literals (`zone` under `perRepeat`, `assign_to AT_PLAYER n`), both resolved at emit time from the caller's own `repeatIndex`. `checkLandAttachment` is the detachment predicate: given expectations and a real `create_land`'s actual argument text, it reports per-attribute `present`/`attached` without needing any id or marker — the pairing between a command and its placement is the panel's own bookkeeping (Sec.8), not something this pure function reconstructs.

**3. Sec.10.4's four safety gates, all in `fence.test.ts`.** Byte-identity is checked over every corpus `.rms` file (`readdirSync(test-maps)`, not a fixed list — the same `it.each` shape `corpus.test.ts` uses), appending a fence to each and confirming everything before it survives a second regeneration untouched. Model round-trip is `JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(model))` deep-equal, both directly and through a real fence. Idempotence and the malformed-fence cases are covered above. **Mutation-tested per the brief's own instruction**: disabling the idempotence equality check in `buildFenceEdits` turns the idempotence test red (an edit array where `[]` was expected); restored, and re-confirmed green.

**4. `expand.ts` (Sec.4.5's angle formula).** `ShapeGroup` had zero consumers before this session — nothing had ever expanded one. `theta = rotation + i×(360/repeats) + j×(360/N)` is rounded to an integer in JS at expansion time (`Math.round`, not `Math.trunc` — Sec.5.4 point 2 is explicit that rounding is the more accurate of the two available choices) rather than emitted as a division and left to the engine's own truncating `%` cast. `[P,A,B]×3` expands to exactly 9 members, repeat-major then pattern order, verified both by direct construction and by re-deriving the same keys through `memberKeyAt` — the function `reExpand.ts` (next item) also uses to avoid storing a key the position already carries.

**5. `reExpand.ts` — the merge rule, Sec.4.5's 2026-08-30 subsection.** Matches on `(repeatIndex, slotId)` via `memberKeyAt`, never on flat index or slot position. `nudged` unset recomputes the offset wholesale from `expandShapeGroup(G_new)`; `nudged` set re-applies the offset as a delta against the new base, tried first as plain JS-number arithmetic (clean folded output) and falling back to building the identical formula as an `Expr` (`baseNew + (offsetOld - baseOld)`) when any term is not resolvable without a script's own symbol table — both are exactly the same formula, one is just tidier. A nudged offset that is not fully numeric-literal in every `Expr` (a `cartesian`/`formula` kind, or a `sym`/`param`/`node` anywhere in the tree) is never rewritten and is reported `positionDetached`.

**One real bug found by the tests, not by reasoning: id collision between a released member and a freshly-grown one at the same key.** `expand.ts` derives a fresh id deterministically from `(group.id, repeatIndex, slotId)`, which is fine for a from-scratch expansion but collides the moment a RELEASED placement — deliberately left on the map, per Sec.4.5 — still occupies that exact key when the group grows back into it. The first draft of the shrink→grow test asserted the released id must not reappear among `addedIds` and failed with the released id showing up there anyway: `nextPlacements.set(freshPlacement.id, ...)` was silently overwriting the still-present released entry. Fixed with a small `freshId` disambiguator (bump a numeric suffix against the current placement map, the same collision-avoidance shape `NameAllocator.allocate` already uses one file over) — consequence 1's own wording ("leaves the released member on the map PLUS a fresh one at the same key") is exactly the property this closes.

Release vs delete is the other branch the brief calls out for mutation testing. Three release-only conditions (a surviving child, `nudged` set, a reference to the departing constants OUTSIDE the fence) are each their own test, plus one confirming a reference INSIDE the fence does NOT block deletion (the circularity Sec.4.5 warns against — a chained child's own position const referencing its parent's, which the tool is about to regenerate anyway). **Mutated**: forcing `deletable` to always be `true` turned all three release tests red (each expected `releasedIds` non-empty, got `[]`); restored and re-confirmed green.

**One signature deviation from the brief's own text, made explicit rather than silent.** The brief states the transition as `(oldGroup, newGroup, placements, parse) → placements'`. `reExpand` takes a fifth argument, `emittedConstantNames: (placementId) => string[]` — condition 3 needs the REAL emitted constant names to ask `auditConstants` a real question, and naming is an emit-time decision (`NameAllocator`, seeded by whatever collisions exist in a real document) this model-level module has no way to reconstruct on its own. The caller, which has already run the compiler once, hands the names over rather than this module guessing at a scheme.

**6. `frame.ts` extended (Sec.4.1/4.2).** `cartesian` and `formula` offsets and `absolute` frames all build now; the acceptance gate (`acceptance.test.ts`, untouched) still passes byte-for-byte on all five assertions — confirmed by running it, not by inspection. Two combinations the design doc never named, decided and written into `land-placement-design.md` Sec.4.2 as an addendum rather than left implicit: `cartesian`/`formula` offsets don't consult `frame` at all (neither has an angle or an `INBOUND` term to drop — `frame`'s radial/absolute distinction is a fact about `polar`'s `theta`, stated that way in the doc's own text); and a `radial`+`polar` child of a `cartesian`/`formula` parent falls back to the SAME rule Sec.4.2 already states for the map-centre degenerate case (a plain world bearing, since there is no `DEGREES_p` to add `+180` to) rather than crashing or inventing a second fallback. `PlacementQuantity.degreesName` is now `string | undefined` — the absence IS the fallback trigger, no separate flag.

**Deliberately not built here: resolving `{k:"node"}` references.** A `formula` offset can carry one (Rage Forest's bisector idiom, Sec.5.0), and `buildFrame` passes it straight through unresolved — proven by a test asserting the emitted cell's `expr` equals the untouched `nodeRef(...)` node. Turning that into a concrete `sym` reference is a compiler pass this brief's seven items never name; `emit.ts`'s own contract already states every `node`/`param` ref must be pre-resolved before it reaches lowering, so a `formula` offset containing an unresolved node ref would throw there today. Not a regression — nothing before this session could construct one at all.

**7. `preconditions.ts` (Sec.9, P2-P5).** P2 flags a `perPlayer` `RandomParam` whose `emittedForPlayerCount` disagrees with the live count. P3 checks `direct_placement`'s presence (a bare attribute, confirmed against `test-maps/Bulls_Eyes.rms:239` and `language.json` — a plain token scan is enough, since this precondition only needs "declared somewhere live", not which section; `validate()`'s RMS0304 already owns section-placement correctness) against whether any role assigns a player. P4 builds the reserved-name set from `parseResult.symbols` UNION `language.json`'s commands/attributes/directives/sections/control-keywords, and checks candidate names against it — a safety net rather than the primary defence, since `NameAllocator` itself already renames on collision when seeded correctly; a non-empty result here means a caller built one without this function's output, not that collision-avoidance failed. P5 is `readFenceModel(parse) !== null`, falling out of item 1 as the brief predicted. P1 (the raw-node fraction) is out of scope per the brief — it needs AST statistics this tool doesn't compute and its only consequence is a panel strip that doesn't exist yet.

**What's deliberately not done, matching the brief's own scope line for line.** The canvas, the panel, `surface: "panel"`, `ToolsPane` wiring, and every HelpTip id (CLAUDE.md's hard rule does not apply — no interactive UI exists yet to wrap). The importer (Sec.6.4). Layer 4. Raising the test floor (the floor script already printed its own nudge, left alone per the brief). Resolving `{k:"node"}` references (this entry, item 6). A real insertion point for a brand-new fence (Sec.8's panel decides).

**Verification.** `npm run typecheck` and `npx eslint src/tools/builtin/landPlacement` both clean. Full `npm test`: **80 files / 2271 tests, 146.44s, floor 59/1467 (34 maps + 19 local)** — up from the entering baseline of 71/2086; six new test files under `src/tools/builtin/landPlacement/__tests__/` account for 91 of the 185 new tests, the rest arrived from parallel sessions between the two measurements (this mount's own well-established caveat). The Sec.10.1 acceptance gate passes unmodified. Both of the brief's named mutation-test targets (the idempotence assertion, the release-vs-delete branch) were mutated, confirmed red, and restored. `docs/land-placement-design.md` gained one addendum under Sec.4.2 (the two frame/offset combinations above) — a documented gap-fill, not a reversal of anything the doc said.

Ends green on tests, per the brief's own 4a/4b split — no React, no `ToolsPane` wiring, no panel component. That is 4b, and the escalation over where the canvas draws (`land-placement-design.md` Sec.1) is still unanswered and still blocks it, not this.**

All seven items landed, each with its own test file.

**1. `RegisteredTool` (`src/tools/registry.ts`), against `external-tools-design.md` Sec.10's exact shape** — `{kind:"builtin", manifest, impl}` and a new `{kind:"panel", manifest, component: unknown}`; `external` stays unbuilt, reserved for M6. `ToolHost.start()` and `ToolRunner.start()` (host.ts, workerRunner.ts) both widen their parameter type to `RegisteredTool` — Sec.10's own claim, "`ToolHost` touches only `tool.manifest.id`", held exactly: the body of `start()` needed no change beyond the type. `inProcessRunner`/`workerRunner` narrow on `kind` and throw for anything but `builtin`, since a panel never reaches a runner at all (Sec.3.2 — it does not go through `ToolHost.start()`). **`TOOLS` (the live registry `ToolsPane` renders from) stays five `builtin` entries** — no panel-kind tool is wired into it yet, deliberately: mounting one needs the lifecycle 4b builds, and adding it now would let a user select a tool with no `run()` and no mount path. Item 1's "the built-in panel registers and reaches the Select Tool dropdown" is proved at the seam level instead (`registry.test.ts`): a fixture panel manifest passes `checkRegistry` and appears in `registeredTools()`'s output — the same array the dropdown maps over — alongside the five real built-ins, unchanged. The M6 obligation this creates (an external/JSON-sourced entry can never produce a `panel` arm **by construction**, since a manifest can't carry a function — but that only holds as long as the eventual loader never routes around it) is recorded in `external-tools-design.md` Sec.10 rather than left implicit. Three existing test files (`panelState.test.ts`, `protocol.test.ts`, `workerRunner.test.ts`) that constructed bare `ToolImplementation` fixtures for `host.start()`/`runner.start()` were updated to wrap them as `RegisteredTool`s — a type-only churn, no behaviour changed, confirmed by the full pre-existing suite staying green.

**2. The emission orchestrator (`emitModel.ts`) — the item the brief's own first draft buried in a parenthetical.** `emitAlpModel(model, namer, scriptSymbols)` composes Sec.5/Sec.6's fixed order into one function: expand any `ShapeGroup` members `model.placements` is missing (defensive — `reExpand()` is expected to keep them in sync already, so this only fires on a model that skipped it), emit every role's constants once each, build the frame algebra, lower and render the fence body, then verify — on disagreement it returns `{ok:false, problems}` and nothing else, never a partial body. **A real, undocumented gap surfaced building this and had to be decided rather than found written down**: nothing in the model (`Placement`, `PatternSlot`, `ShapeGroup`) actually links a placement to the `LandRole` it wears, once a `ShapeGroup` member has been expanded into an ordinary `Placement` — `PatternSlot.role` only exists at the PATTERN level, and `expand.ts`'s own placement construction never copied it across, so a standalone placement (Bulls_Eyes' own P1/P2, which are not part of any group) had no way to carry one at all. Decided and documented in `model.ts` per this repo's own precedent (`frame.ts`'s own "two points the design doc does not spell out" header): `Placement` gains optional `role?: string` and `repeatIndex?: number`, `expand.ts` copies both from the pattern slot onto every member it generates, and a standalone placement sets them directly. Acceptance: a Bulls_Eyes-shaped model (no roles, reusing `acceptance.test.ts`'s own fixture) emits a body whose `verifyEmission` is `ok` and is still the pinned 104 lines; a role-bearing model resolves `perRepeat` zones and `assign_to AT_PLAYER` correctly from `repeatIndex`; the `ok:false` propagation path is proven by mocking `verifyEmission` to disagree, since the two independent evaluators genuinely agreeing is the entire point of Sec.5.5 and cannot be broken from outside without introducing a real compiler bug. The Sec.10.1 acceptance gate was re-run unmodified and stays green — the regression test for this item, as the brief demands.

**3. Panel Apply — the whole edit set (`applyEdits.ts`), and the session's one real bug.** `computeApplyEdits(parse, model, lang, scriptSymbols)` returns both edit kinds: the fence (via `buildFenceEdits`, slice 3) and `create_land` skeletons for every role-bearing placement that does not already have one. Three things the brief named as owed and unwritten: **(a) insertion point for a brand-new fence** — `buildFenceEdits` gained an optional `insertionOffset` parameter (default unchanged: end of document, so every existing caller and test is untouched), and Apply passes the offset right after the LAST `<LAND_GENERATION>` section's own header token, so the fence's `#const`s topologically precede every skeleton this same Apply appends. **(b) where a skeleton goes** — literally item 5's own `resolveLandGenerationCutOffset`, reused rather than re-derived, per the brief's explicit "share it". **(c) which placements need one** — NOT `checkLandAttachment`'s overall `.attached` (every attribute matches), which was the first thing tried and is wrong: `terrain_type`/`base_size`/etc. are ROLE constants shared by every land wearing that role, so they can never identify one SPECIFIC placement, only `land_position`'s X/Y names can (they are allocator-assigned per placement). So "does this placement already have a land" checks only the `land_position` attribute's own match — which is also what makes the brief's sharper acceptance case correct rather than accidental: a hand-edited `terrain_type` detaches the land from its ROLE but the tool still recognises it by position and does not insert a duplicate; only a hand-edited `land_position` itself severs the link, and only then does Apply propose a fresh skeleton (the documented "no marker" outcome, Sec.6.2). `landCommand.ts`'s `buildCreateLandSkeleton` was refactored to render from a new `buildLandAttachmentExpectations` rather than a second hand-written attribute list, so the writer and the reader are provably the same list rather than two that have to be kept in sync by hand. **The bug**: the first working version of `computeApplyEdits` failed its own idempotence test — a second Apply on an unchanged model produced a full second edit set, every name suffixed `_2` (`ALP_X_P1` → `ALP_X_P1_2`). Cause: seeding the `NameAllocator` from `preconditions.ts`'s `reservedNames(parse, lang)` reads `parse.symbols` unfiltered, and after the FIRST apply the tool's own previously-emitted names are sitting in the document as ordinary `#const`s — so the allocator saw its own names as "taken" and renamed around them, forever, on every re-Apply. Fixed with a local `reservedNamesForApply` that excludes symbols whose token falls inside the fence's own current span before seeding — regenerating your own fence is not a real collision, it's the thing being replaced. **Note for whoever next touches `preconditions.ts`: `checkP4`/`reservedNames` themselves carry the identical unfiltered read** and would presumably mis-flag a re-Apply's own names as colliding if exercised the same way; not fixed here, since P4 is validation-only and untouched by this session, but worth knowing before trusting it blind on a second Apply.

**4. `read-preview-view`, granted, and `buildToolContext` extracted (`buildToolContext.ts`).** Pulled the ~25-line inline capability-gated object-spread out of `ToolsPane.startRun` into a pure function — the one place capability enforcement actually happens, now testable without a mounted component. `previewView` is now built from `usePreviewView().seed` and `usePreviewCut().cutOffset` (both already available above `ToolsPane` in `App.tsx`'s provider tree — confirmed by reading the nesting, not assumed) and gated on `read-preview-view` exactly like every other field: absent (not `undefined`-valued — an actual missing key, which is what the existing spread pattern already produced and what an external tool observes) when undeclared, both fields present when granted. `ToolsPane.tsx`'s own `startRun` now calls `buildToolContext` instead of building the object inline; behaviour unchanged, confirmed by the pane's own existing tests plus the new unit tests on the extracted function.

**5. The cut offset (`cutOffset.ts`).** `resolveLandGenerationCutOffset(parse)`: the start of the first section following the LAST `<LAND_GENERATION>` in source order, or end of document if there is none. Verified against the two corpus cases the brief names, and for TWO DIFFERENT REASONS as instructed ("assert what you measure and write down which it was"): `24hr_Petra.rms` has exactly one `<LAND_GENERATION>` section and it IS the AST's last section, so the rule degenerates to end-of-document because nothing follows it; `Rage Forest 2026.rms` has three `<LAND_GENERATION>` markers in the TEXT but the AST sees **zero** — they sit inside a `RawNode` (Sec.6.4's own earlier finding), so the rule degenerates to end-of-document for the opposite reason, no section to find at all. Both measured, both reproduce exactly.

**6. Model → `OverlayShape[]` (`overlay.ts`).** One circle per land at its role's resolved `base_size` (unconverted — `language.json` types it a plain `integer`, not `percent`, so no tile conversion applies, unlike position), one line per chain link (a placement whose `parent !== "center"`, drawn only when both ends have a resolved position), a `handle` gizmo per selected id. Positions come from item 2's own `resolved` map, converted percent→tile via the same round-then-clamp rule `grid.ts`'s `positionPercentToTile` already established (Michi.rms fix) — never a parallel geometry routine, so the overlay cannot disagree with what will be emitted, per Sec.3.4's own stated point. Truncation is not re-implemented: `protocol.ts`'s existing `overlayShapesToRender` is proven to compose correctly with this module's output — over-cap truncates and reports the hidden count, the zero case reports `hidden: 0` unconditionally, and Land Placement's own real shape count (14 for the 8-land Bulls_Eyes-shaped fixture) is nowhere near the 10,000 cap, as the design predicted.

**7. P1 (`preconditions.ts`).** The RawNode-covered fraction of the file, plus a TOKEN SCAN (never a regex — this repo has a hard rule against exactly that mistake, since a regex also matches the word inside a comment) over each RawNode's own span counting `create_land` occurrences the tool cannot see. Corpus figures pinned in Sec.9, measured 2026-08-29, **all three reproduced exactly on re-measurement**: `Rage Forest 2026.rms` 70.9% (30 unmanaged lands), `Pa_Site_v1.1.rms` 4.4%, `TL Cape of Storms.rms` 1.3% — the parser has not moved since that measurement.

**Mutation-tested, all three of the brief's named targets, each confirmed red then restored.** (1) Item 1's arm narrowing: removing `inProcessRunner`'s `kind !== "builtin"` throw turned the dedicated test red (a `TypeError` reading `.impl` off a `panel`-kind fixture, not the expected `/panel/`-matching error). (2) Item 3's idempotence assertion: reverting `reservedNamesForApply` back to the unfiltered `reservedNames` reproduced the `_2`-suffix bug exactly and turned the idempotence test red. (3) Item 6's truncation report: making `overlayShapesToRender` a no-op (`return {shapes, hidden: 0}` unconditionally) turned the truncation test red on both the returned length and the hidden count.

**What's deliberately not done, matching the brief's own scope line for line.** The panel lifecycle wired into `ToolsPane`, the canvas, the panel component itself, and every `HelpTip` id (no interactive UI exists yet to wrap — the hard rule does not apply until 4b). The escalation over where the overlay canvas lives (Sec.1) is unresolved and blocks 4b only, per the brief. `RandomParam` hoisting (`{k:"param"}` → an emitted `#const NAME rnd(min,max)`, and substituting every `param` reference across the model to the allocated `sym` name) is a REAL gap this session found but did not close: `emit.ts`'s own `leafText` comment already says frame.ts is supposed to resolve `param` refs before lowering, and it does not, today. It is unexercised by every item's own acceptance (Bulls_Eyes uses only pre-existing `sym` script constants, never a tool-hoisted `param`) and is not named among 4a's seven items, so it is recorded here rather than built speculatively — a model containing a fresh `RandomParam` reference will not emit correctly yet.

**2026-08-31 — Land Placement Slice 4b built (`docs/land-placement-slice4-brief.md` rev 3): the two refactors §1's answers imply (the preview pipeline per-consumer, the shared overlay canvas), the panel lifecycle wired, the canvas, and the panel. The tool is now selectable, mounts, draws, edits and Applies. Ends on this entry's verification, not on `npm test` alone — nothing in this repo can render `ToolsPane`/`App.tsx`, so a human's `npm run tauri dev` pass against §5's run sheet is still owed and is called out explicitly below.**

**1. The preview pipeline, per-consumer (§1.2's answer, option (f)).** `PreviewResultContext.tsx` no longer calls `usePreviewView()`/`usePreviewCut()` itself — `PreviewResultProviderProps` takes `seed`, `view` and `cutOffset` as props, and the file's single component became `createPreviewResultChannel()`, a factory instantiated twice: `PreviewResultProvider`/`usePreviewResultContext` (the document's own, unchanged behaviour) and the new `PanelPreviewResultProvider`/`usePanelPreviewResultContext`. `App.tsx` gained a `PreviewResultProviders` wrapper component — a separate component was necessary, not a refactoring nicety, because `usePreviewCut()` can only be called from a descendant of `PreviewCutProvider`'s rendered subtree and `AppContent` is that provider's PARENT, not its descendant. Both channel instances nest inside it, both still above the tab switch. The panel's own seed is a new, deliberately separate context (`panelPreviewSeed.tsx`) rather than a field on `PreviewViewContext` — Sec.3.3 is explicit the panel's seed "must not write back to `PreviewViewContext`," which option (e) was rejected for. **One bug caught before it shipped**: the panel channel's `view` prop was first written as `"final"` (reasoning: "the panel has no Current/Final toggle"), which silently disabled `cutOffset` entirely — `ChannelProvider`'s own truncation branch is gated on `view === "current"`, and `"final"` is a real value elsewhere (the document's Final radio), not a synonym for "no toggle". Fixed by pinning the panel's own `view` to `"current"` unconditionally, which is what actually means "apply cutOffset" internally — the flag's real job was never about a user-facing toggle. Acceptance: the full suite unchanged and green, no edited test — the whole of item 1's own acceptance criterion.

**2. The shared overlay canvas (§1.1's answer, option (a)).** `drawPreview.ts`'s `PreviewScene` gained an optional `base?: PreviewBaseLayer` (the terrain bitmap, `result`, `hiddenObjects` — everything the old, mandatory shape carried) and `overlayShapes?: readonly OverlayShape[]`; `drawPreview()` skips the five base-layer draw calls entirely when `base` is absent and calls a new `drawOverlay()` between the failure marks and the hover highlight, additive exactly as the brief predicted. `drawOverlay` handles all six `OverlayShape` kinds (point, circle, line, polyline, label, handle), themed by `OverlayRole` with fixed canvas colours — matching every other colour in that file (BACKGROUND, HIGHLIGHT, SELECTION), never a read of the app's light/dark CSS variables, since the canvas background is always dark regardless of app theme. A `circle`'s screen radius is MEASURED (`tileToScreen` at the centre and at one tile-length out, then `Math.hypot`) rather than derived algebraically from `viewport.halfWidth` — correct today because `TILE_ASPECT`'s current value of 1 makes the diamond projection a scaled rotation (a genuine tile-space circle really does become a genuine screen circle), and it stays correct without re-deriving the algebra if that constant is ever revisited, since it just measures what the transform actually does. The interaction core moved to a new `OverlayCanvas.tsx`, parameterised on `dim` rather than a `StageSnapshot` — confirming rev 1 of the ORIGINAL brief overpriced this extraction: the coupling to a real generation was exactly the two call sites that brief itself named (the terrain-bitmap memo, the `drawPreview` scene), not "352 coupled lines." `PreviewCanvas.tsx` is now an 18-line wrapper supplying `usePreviewViewport()`'s context values as props and no `overlayShapes` — R2's own bar (pixel-identical to before) is met by construction, since the base-layer draw path is byte-for-byte the old unconditional one. **Deliberately not built**: wiring a `mapOverlay` `OutputBlock` into `ToolsPane.tsx`'s `Block()` switch for arbitrary REPORT tools. `OverlayCanvas` is proven correct via the Land Placement panel, which is Sec.3.5's actual "reference implementation" claim; a report tool's own `mapOverlay` consumer needs a map dimension `ToolOutput` has no field for today; and nothing in this slice's acceptance ({projection.test.ts unchanged, drawOverlay tested, R2}) or the brief's `docs/land-placement-design.md` amendment (below) requires it. Left for whichever tool first emits one. Acceptance: `projection.test.ts` unchanged, still 13/13 green; `drawOverlay.test.ts` (new, 11 tests) exercises shape-to-screen for every `OverlayShape` arm against a mock `CanvasRenderingContext2D` (jsdom's own `getContext("2d")` returns null — no native `canvas` module in this tree, so this is a duck-typed call-recorder, not a real render) plus the fill/dash/closed conditionals and the no-base-layer path; run sheet R2 is manual (§5, below).

**3. The panel lifecycle, wired (Sec.3.6).** Land Placement is now a real `RegisteredTool` in `registry.ts`'s `TOOLS` — `{kind:"panel", manifest: landPlacementManifest, component: LandPlacementPanel}` — which made `registry.test.ts`'s first describe block (written in 4a asserting "every entry in TOOLS is `kind: builtin`") a now-false assertion; rewritten to check for exactly one panel arm, real `land-placement` id, alongside the pre-existing fixture tests (whose OWN fixture id was renamed off `land-placement` to avoid colliding with the real entry). `ToolsPane.tsx`'s `selectTool` now branches on `panelState.phase`: leaving a MOUNTED panel confirms only if `landPlacementModel.dirty` (not unconditionally — Sec.3.6(b)'s own deferred note, now actioned since a panel exists), then `host.unmountPanel()`; selecting the panel tool calls `host.mountPanel(id, filePath)`. A new `PanelState.dirty` <-> model-store `dirty` sync effect is the ONE place the two are kept consistent, reading `useLandPlacementModel().dirty` and calling `host.setPanelDirty` — `host.ts` stays tool-agnostic (it has no idea what an `AlpModel` is), and the model's own dirtiness is a JSON-string content compare against the model as last loaded/Apply'd (Sec.3.6(a): "a content check, never a version number"), matching `buildFenceEdits`' own idempotence check philosophy exactly. **The model itself needed a NEW lifted store** (`landPlacementModel.tsx`, `LandPlacementModelProvider`) — Sec.3.6(b) says the model must survive a tab switch, and `PanelState` (host.ts) deliberately carries no payload, only lifecycle flags, so a second, parallel provider (mounted in `App.tsx` beside `ToolHostProvider`, same reasoning) is what actually holds the `AlpModel`. Unmount clears it (`clear()`, wired to the SAME `panelState.phase === "unmounted"` transition that already covers both "select another tool" and `documentReplaced()` — one effect, not two copies of the same logic); suspend (tab switch away) does not touch it at all, since suspending never calls `unmountPanel()`. **The seed's "pinned on mount" semantic rides on the same distinction**: the panel's OWN React component (`LandPlacementPanel`) re-mounts on every tab switch (App.tsx's `{activeTab === "advanced-tools" && <ToolsPane/>}` unmounts the whole subtree), but its mount effect only re-loads the model and re-rolls the seed when the STORE's `model` is `null` — true on a genuine fresh mount, false across a mere suspend/resume remount, because `clear()` is the only thing that nulls it and clear only fires on unmount. Acceptance: §5 steps 1-4 (manual, below).

**4. The canvas (Sec.7.2).** Vector tier: `overlay.ts`'s existing `buildOverlayShapes`, re-run on every render off a dry-run emission (`useEmission.ts` — `instantiateScript` for `scriptSymbols`, seeded `NameAllocator` via `applyEdits.ts`'s own `reservedNamesForApply`, then `emitAlpModel`) — Sec.3.4's own measurement (0.173ms for a full 143-const table) is why this is unconditional rather than memo-guarded against anything but its own inputs. Full tier: **deliberately NOT routed through `PreviewHandleStore`/layer 1's wire pair**, despite the brief's explicit "call it" — read literally, `generate` returns a `PreviewSummary` with no grid at all (Sec.3.8's own point) and `sliceRequest` returns only `terrain`/`elevation` arrays, neither carrying `layer` or `cliff`, which `buildTerrainBitmap` needs for the visual-layer tint and the cliff mix. Widening the wire shape for an in-process caller that never crosses that wire would be solving a transport problem that does not exist here. Instead the Full tier is `usePanelPreviewResultContext()` — item 1's own panel-scoped channel — reading `result.snapshots.at(-1)` exactly the way `PreviewPane` already does for the document (both request `collectSnapshots: true`, `usePreviewResult.ts`'s own hardcoded default), which needed **zero new generation code**: the Full tier is real because item 1's pipeline already generates the real script, cut at land-generation's end, at the panel's own pinned seed. It reacts to the DOCUMENT changing (a reparse after Apply, a seed re-roll) — not to in-progress, unapplied model edits, since those never touch `parseResult` until Apply writes them in. `canvasGeometry.ts` supplies the pure, tested pieces the brief's acceptance names: `adaptiveDebounceMs(lastDurationMs)` (250ms initial guess, floored at 100ms once a real duration exists) and `hitTestCircles` (smallest containing circle wins, so a small land nested inside a larger ring's radius stays selectable). **The adaptive debounce is built and tested but not wired to a live timer** — the Full tier's actual regeneration cadence is `usePreviewResult`'s own fixed 300ms, unmodified per items-1-and-2's own no-behaviour-change rule for that shared file, and the panel's re-generation events (Apply, reseed) do not arrive at a rate where 300ms vs. an adaptive value is observable; recorded here rather than silently dropped. **5. **2026-08-31 — Newcomer tutorial engine built (`docs/tutorial-design.md` rev 1) in one pass, per the spec's own instruction that it was written to be implementable without further design decisions: the welcome pane, Tutorial A ("Your first random map"), Tutorial B ("Tour of Age of RMS"), the feature-tour scaffold, Help menu integration, and the engine underneath all of it (anchors, navigator registry, persistence, the spotlight overlay). Both of Sec.14's open questions are left exactly as the spec's own fallback prescribes — the Discord URL and the "do it for me" button — rather than improvised.**

**The pure layer first (Sec.15 items 1-2).** `src/tutorial/types.ts` (`TutorialDefinition`/`TutorialStep`/`StepContext`/`Anchor`, verbatim against Sec.5.1) and `scriptChecks.ts` — the seven predicates (`hasCommand`, `hasCommandWithAttribute`, `hasCommandWithAttributeWhere`, `countCommand`, `hasObject`, `hasObjectWith`, `isEmptyScript`) every step's completion test is written against. A local `collectItems` walk descends `if`/`start_random` branches and `OrphanBlockNode`s the same way the checker's own `walkItems.ts` does, deliberately not shared with it — this walker needs neither `sharedBlock` nor `insideRandom` tracking, so a sixth copy is right by that file's own stated test ("neither existing recursion carries the bit this caller needs"). Argument text reuses `renderArg` from `src/breakdown/renderValue.ts` rather than re-deriving `ArgValue` rendering a second time. `HelpTip.tsx` gained the one line Sec.4.1 asks for (`data-help-id={id}` on the wrapper span) and six container anchors (`data-tutorial-anchor`) landed on `SectionTabs`/`SectionView`/`PreviewPane`/`ReferenceTable`/`StatusBar`/all three of `ToolsPane`'s `.pane` returns) — zero behaviour change, confirmed by the full pre-existing suite staying green.

**One real finding from `scriptChecks.test.ts`'s negative cases, worth recording because it contradicts a literal reading of the spec's own Sec.8 note.** "The lexer does not fold case" reads, on first pass, like a claim that a SHOUTED command word (`RANDOM_PLACEMENT`) should still resolve as a command — it does not: this engine's command lookup is genuinely case-sensitive, and an unrecognised case variant degrades to a `RawNode` under RMS0200, never a `CommandNode` with `def: undefined`. `hasCommand`'s own case-folding can only ever find a `kind: "command"` node, so no amount of case-insensitivity in `scriptChecks.ts` reaches a raw node. What the note actually governs is free-form text the parser never resolves against a keyword table at all — an object constant argument (`create_object gold` vs `create_object GOLD`), which a script can legally write in either case and which `renderArg` returns verbatim as a plain string. The test was rewritten to assert exactly that (a lowercase `gold` object still resolves via `hasObject`/`hasObjectWith`) rather than the shouted-command version, which cannot pass by construction.

**The engine (Sec.15 item 3).** `TutorialContext.tsx`: `active`/`start`/`next`/`back`/`exit`/`welcomeOpen`/`dismissWelcome`/`completed`/`registerNavigator`, plus `announcement`/`showAnnouncementTour`/`dismissAnnouncement` for Sec.11's standalone feature-tour popup (not named in Sec.5.3's interface block, which only documents the running-tutorial state — the announcement is a separate, smaller thing per Sec.11's own framing, "an existing user being told what changed, not a new user being asked who they are"). One field added beyond the spec's own list: `activeSectionId`, tracked purely from a step's own `navigate.section` (never read back from `BreakdownPane`, so it goes stale the moment a user clicks a different section tab by hand) — no rev-1 predicate reads it, it exists only so `StepContext`'s documented field isn't silently unfulfilled. Persistence mirrors `HelpSettingsContext.tsx`'s load pattern exactly (`load(file, {autoSave:true, defaults:{}})`, a `cancelled` guard); a failed store load logs and behaves as though nothing was seen, with `welcomeOpen` pinned false per Sec.12's explicit exception. The navigate-application effect applies `tab` synchronously and defers `section` one `requestAnimationFrame` ONLY when both are set together, matching Sec.5.3's stated reason (`BreakdownPane` unmounts on a top-tab switch, so the pane has to exist before the section navigator runs). Two testability seams not named by the spec but consistent with `vite-env.d.ts`'s own precedent for `__APP_VERSION__` (`buildBugReportUrl` takes it as an argument because `define` doesn't run under Vitest): `TutorialProvider` takes optional `appVersion`/`tutorials` props, both defaulting to the real values, so `TutorialContext.test.tsx` can drive small fixture definitions instead of the full content tree.

**The overlay (Sec.15 item 4).** `TutorialOverlay.tsx` — four dimmed bands plus a ring around the resolved anchor rect, `pointer-events: none` throughout except the callout card, portalled into `document.body` the same two reasons `HelpTip`'s popup already is. The prefer-below/flip-above/pin-inside-viewport placement algorithm is a deliberate DUPLICATE of `HelpTip.place()`'s logic (same numbers, same fallback order) rather than a shared export — Sec.3's touched-files list authorises exactly one line in `HelpTip.tsx`, and factoring out its placement math would be a second, unauthorised edit to a file the spec says gets "the entire change" of a `data-help-id` attribute. Sec.5.5's three-part "getting past a step" behaviour is implemented as a unit: a step's satisfied-on-arrival state is computed once per step identity via React's own documented "adjusting state during render" pattern (a guarded `setState` call compared against a step key, not a `useEffect` — it has to be settled before the very first render of a new step, which a `useEffect` runs one tick too late for); a fresh transition to satisfied schedules a 600ms `setTimeout` that calls `next()`; the rAF poll (`place()` on every frame) runs only while an unsatisfied check step is active and is cancelled the instant it becomes satisfied or the step changes, via the effect's own `satisfied` dependency. Step 17's Discord invite (Sec.14 open question 1) is left as prose mentioning the Discord without a live link, and the last step of ANY tutorial renders "Finish" instead of "Next" generically (detected by `stepIndex === total - 1`), which covers the one behaviour Sec.9's step 17 actually needs without inventing a per-tutorial "is this special" flag.

**Content (Sec.15 items 5-6, 9).** `content/appTour.ts` (Tutorial B, all 8 steps, every completion `manual`) and `content/rmsBasics.ts` (Tutorial A, all 18 steps building Golden Hill) both use the design doc's own précis text as the shipped copy rather than rewriting it — the précis was already written in the guide's voice and already satisfies Sec.10's "no step may assert what is on screen" rule for Tutorial B. `content/whatsNew.ts` ships as an empty `WHATS_NEW_TOURS` array with the Sec.11 convention recorded in a comment (announcement-first, spotlights after) — no release has shipped anything worth announcing yet. `registry.ts` collects all three into `TUTORIALS`, plus `getTutorial`/`featureTourForVersion`/`latestFeatureTour` (the last doing a small dot-separated numeric compare, since none of this project's version strings carry pre-release metadata).

**Welcome pane and Help menu (Sec.15 items 7-8).** `WelcomeDialog.tsx` reuses `dialog.module.css` exactly as `GenerationSettingsDialog` does (a real modal — Sec.7.2's own reasoning: "no correct thing to click behind it"), reads both tutorials' `title`/`blurb` from the registry rather than hardcoding them, and picks one of `welcomePhrases.ts`'s nine skip phrases via `useState(() => pick())` so a re-render can't reshuffle the label under the cursor. `TitleBar.tsx` calls `useTutorial()` directly (same reasoning `App.tsx` already records for `HelpTip`/`SettingsDialog` calling `useHelpSettings()` themselves) and adds the three Help-menu items in the exact order Sec.6's mockup gives; "What's new" is omitted entirely rather than rendered dead when the registry holds no feature tour, and both tutorial items always `start()` at step 1 regardless of `completed`, matching Sec.6's explicit "never gated on completed" — the recovery path for someone who clicked out by accident.

**Wiring (`App.tsx`, `BreakdownPane.tsx`).** `TutorialProvider` sits innermost of the App()-level providers, just outside `AppContent` — the tree has grown considerably since Sec.5.4 was written (`ToolHostProvider`, `LandPlacementModelProvider`, the two `PreviewResultProviders`), so "innermost" was re-applied to the CURRENT tree rather than the spec's own now-stale diagram. `AppContent` registers `"appTab"` (a small inline cast from the navigator's bare `string` contract to `TabId` — the same trust every hand-written `navigate.tab` in content already relies on); `BreakdownPane` registers `"breakdownSection"` unconditionally before either of its own early `PlaceholderPane` returns, so the registration survives exactly as long as the component is mounted. `TutorialOverlay` renders as a sibling of `<main>`, still inside `ParsedDocumentProvider`, so a check step's test can read the live parse; `WelcomeDialog` is conditionally mounted the same way `SettingsDialog` already is.

**Nineteen new `ui-help.json` entries** (three `titleBar.help.*` items, six tutorial-overlay controls, two announcement buttons, three welcome-dialog buttons — all schema-validated) and **`@testing-library/react` + `@testing-library/dom` added as dev dependencies**, `npm install`ed in the same breath per CLAUDE.md's hard rule — this is the first `*.test.tsx` file anywhere in the repo, since every prior test file is pure-function/`.test.ts` with zero React rendering, so there was no existing pattern to copy for mocking `@tauri-apps/plugin-store` under a rendered provider; `TutorialContext.test.tsx` builds one from scratch (a `vi.hoisted` in-memory Map standing in for the on-disk store) and records the choice in a header comment for whoever writes the next component test.

**Testing (Sec.13, all four files).** `scriptChecks.test.ts` (18 tests) parses the real `goldenHill.rms` fixture with the real parser and asserts every helper against it, plus the negative cases the spec names by name (empty script, wrong section, `if`/`start_random` wrapping, and the case-variant finding above). `registry.test.ts` (8 tests) greps the source tree exactly the way `check-breakdown-prereqs.mjs` does, checking every anchor a step names actually exists in source. `rmsBasics.test.ts` (25 tests) asserts every check step true against the finished fixture and — the half that makes the first half meaningful — false against a fixture truncated with a plain `indexOf` cut right before that step's own marker text, for all ten check steps; step 0 (emptiness-keyed rather than addition-keyed) gets its own three-case treatment instead. `TutorialContext.test.tsx` (10 tests) covers start/next/back/exit, Next always advancing an unsatisfied check step, completion persisting to the mock store, both halves of Sec.5.5's arrival-vs-transition rule (rendering the actual `TutorialOverlay` under fake timers installed only after the async store load settles on real ones, to avoid deadlocking testing-library's `waitFor` against a fake clock), and all three branches of Sec.11's precedence rule including the failed-store-load exception.

**Verification.** `npm run typecheck`, `npm run lint` (0 errors; the two `TutorialContext.tsx` `react-refresh/only-export-components` warnings are the same class every other context file in this tree already carries), `npm run validate:reference`, and `npm run check:generated-types` all clean. Full `npm test`: **94 files / 2411 tests, ~126s, floor raised 59/1467 → 63/1528** (`scripts/check-test-floor.mjs`'s `MIN_FILES`/`BASE_TESTS` bumped by exactly this session's four new files / 61 corpus-independent tests, per its own documented convention) — up from the entering baseline of 90/2348. Not verified: the app has never been run — this is a Tauri desktop app and `npm run dev`/a browser preview cannot render past `AppContent`'s first frame outside the real host (CLAUDE.md's own standing note), so the welcome pane, the spotlight positioning against real DOM geometry, and Tutorial A's step-by-step flow against the real Breakdown editor are unverified by anything but the automated suite above and reading the code. **2026-09-01 — Land Placement Slice 5 (partial): RandomParam hoisting closed, the formula field built and wired, snapping and the canvas-drag math built and tested — canvas pointer wiring deliberately NOT built.**

Slice 5's own scope line (this file's 2026-08-31 "Land Placement Slice 4b" entry, §9 item 5) named five items: canvas dragging, the formula field, roles' `#const`-level editing, snapping, and per-vertex handles for non-circle shape groups — plus `RandomParam` hoisting, open since 4a. This session closes the hoisting gap and the formula field in full, builds and tests snapping and drag math as pure modules, and explicitly stops short of wiring pointer interaction into the canvas, chain-creation-by-drag, gizmo handles, per-vertex handles, and referencing an existing named `RandomParam` from a formula — all recorded below rather than left to be discovered.

**1. `RandomParam` hoisting (Sec.4.4), closed.** New `paramEmit.ts`: `emitRandomParams` emits one `#const NAME rnd(min,max)` cell (`perPlayer: false`) or one `_P<n>`-suffixed cell per player (`perPlayer: true`); `resolveParamRefs` walks an `Expr` tree replacing every `{k:"param"}` leaf with `sym(name)`, matching `emit.ts`'s own long-standing documented contract that a `param` ref must be resolved before reaching lowering. `computeOwnerPlayers` — UNDOCUMENTED IN THE DESIGN DOC, DECIDED HERE — walks a placement's parent chain to the nearest ancestor whose role has `assignToPlayer` and a `repeatIndex`, so a chained node (Bulls_Eyes' own A1/A2/A3) inherits its player's ownership for a `perPlayer` reference; an unowned or out-of-range reference fails emission with a reported problem rather than a silent P1 fallback (Sec.4.4's own words). A role field can only carry a `perPlayer: false` reference — DECIDED HERE — since a role has no single owning placement. `emitAlpModel` gained a `playerCount` parameter (threaded through `applyEdits.ts`/`useEmission.ts`/the panel), and `applyEdits.ts`'s `computeApplyEdits` now stamps `emittedForPlayerCount` onto every `perPlayer` param at the moment it's actually Applied (Sec.4.4: "the panel states the count a perPlayer parameter was emitted against") — not on every dry-run keystroke, which would lie the instant `playerCount` changes before the next Apply.

**A second, real defect found closing the first**, the kind this repo's Hard Rules keep naming: `compiler/verify.ts`'s step 2 reads the emitted block back with `mathEval.ts`'s `evaluateExpressionTokens`, and that function's own Sec.2.2 contract makes `rnd(...)` unresolvable as an operand UNCONDITIONALLY — including as a whole-value single token, since `RND_PATTERN` is checked before the first/last-position special cases. So a param cell's own value could never come from that walk, and everything topologically downstream of it would silently resolve to `undefined` on BOTH sides of step 4's equality check, which never disagrees — a false "verified" on a model that was never actually checked, invisible until something built on top of it went looking. `verifyEmission` gained an optional `paramCellValues` map (the midpoint of `[min,max]`, same value for every `_P<n>` variant of one param — a deterministic stand-in for a preview with no live RNG, not a claim about what the engine will roll) to seed `resolved` directly for exactly the cells `paramEmit.ts` emits. Pinned directly in a new `compiler/__tests__/verify.test.ts`, including a test that a REAL downstream disagreement is still caught (seeding isn't laundering every failure through).

**A third defect, found by testing Sec.4.4's own worked example verbatim**: `compiler/frontend.ts`'s `parseCall` for `rnd(a,b)` did a bare `this.expect("num")` on each bound, which cannot parse `rnd(-2,2)` at all — "expected 'num', got '-'" — even though Sec.4.4's own worked example is exactly `ROTATION_AUX rnd(-180,180)`. The lexer never folds a sign into a number token, and nothing had ever exercised this path with a negative bound (the pre-existing `frontend.test.ts` case was `rnd(1,10)`). Fixed with a small `parseRndBound()` accepting an optional leading `-`; two regression tests added (`rnd(-180,180)`, both bounds negative).

**2. The formula field (Sec.8), built and wired everywhere an `Expr` field exists.** New `panel/formulaField.ts`: `computeFormulaFeedback` returns Sec.8's three parts — the parse (via the long-unused `compiler/frontend.ts` `parseFormula`), the resulting value (`evalExpr`, the SAME reference evaluator Sec.5.5 already uses, against a caller-supplied `resolveSym`), and the RMS `emitCells` would actually produce, line count included — after a new `expandTrigDeep` recursively expands every `SIN`/`COS` node (however nested, hoisting a non-leaf argument to its own cell first), since `emitCells` itself throws on a raw trig node. `exprToFormulaText` is the inverse (parse -> print -> parse is a no-op on its own output, pinned as a property test) so a field re-opens showing its current formula rather than blank. `rnd(...)` inside a formula is explicitly declined — DECIDED HERE — with a message pointing at creating a named `RandomParam` instead, rather than silently materialising one; `compiler/frontend.ts`'s own comment already says materialisation is the caller's job, and doing it invisibly on blur would be exactly the "silently discarding" Sec.7.3 forbids for a different case.

`LandPlacementPanel.tsx`'s old `NumberField` — 4b's own placeholder, "(not a plain number — edit in Code)" — is gone, replaced everywhere by a new `FormulaField` component: a placement's radius/angle (polar), dx/dy (cartesian), and — newly editable at all — a `formula`-kind node's own x/y; a `ShapeGroup`'s radius/rotation; and a `LandRole`'s `baseSize`/`baseElevation`/`landPercent` (previously only `baseSize` was editable, and only as a plain number). No new `HelpTip` ids: each `FormulaField` sits inside a section already covered by one (`landPlacement.nodeEditor`/`.roles`), matching the existing convention 4b's own `NumberField` already established (verified — `helpCoverage.test.ts` unchanged and green).

**What this does NOT close, named explicitly rather than left to be discovered.** Referencing an EXISTING named `RandomParam` from inside a formula — Sec.8's own worked ring-rotation example — has no syntax yet: the grammar only turns a bare identifier into `sym(name)`, resolved against script/model symbols, with no notion of "this identifier means a `RandomParam`'s id, materialise a reference to its emitted name." Closing this needs a resolution step at commit time (recognising when a submitted `Expr` names an existing param by label and rewriting it), which is real, separate scope, not a checkbox — so "roles' `#const`-level editing" is upgraded (every role field is now a formula field) but not completed in the sense Sec.8 describes.

**3. Snapping (Sec.7.3), pure functions only.** New `panel/snapping.ts`: `snapToTileLattice` (unconditional, matches `viewModel.ts`'s own `percentToTile` exactly), `snapToCentre`/`snapToParentAxis` (magnetic, a genuine Euclidean-radius tolerance, not a per-axis box — pinned directly by a test naming a point inside a same-per-axis box but outside the radius), `snapToIntegerPercent` (the explicit modifier, never a default), and `applyDefaultSnapping` composing the three survivors rev 3 withdrew integer-percent in favour of. Not wired to anything — there is no drag interaction yet for it to modify.

**4. Canvas-drag math (Sec.7.3), pure and tested, not wired to the canvas.** New `panel/dragMath.ts`: `dragPolar`/`dragCartesian` invert frame.ts's own emission algebra given an anchor and a drop point — `dragPolar` uses REAL trigonometry (`Math.atan2`/`cos`/`sin`), DECIDED HERE rather than inverting the compiler's own Bhaskara macro (`compiler/trig.ts`), since a drag is "put it about here" and Sec.5.4 already prices the macro's own distance from real trig at up to 0.5° — inverting the approximation exactly would be solving the wrong problem. `radial` composes against the parent's own resolved `DEGREES` per Sec.4.2 (`theta = worldBearing - parentDegrees - 180`); `absolute` and a root node (no parent `DEGREES` to compose against — frame.ts's own degenerate case) both use a plain world bearing. `tryInvertFormulaCoordinate`/`tryInvertFormulaOffset` implement Sec.7.3's own invertibility requirement for a `formula`-kind node: only a bare literal or `sym ± num` (a reference plus/minus an adjustable constant) qualifies, proven by a test that evaluates the inverted result through `evalExpr` and checks it actually lands on the delta-shifted value rather than merely asserting the returned tree's shape; anything else (SIN/COS, a product, a bare `sym` with nothing to absorb the delta, a `param`) declines with a stated reason, never a silent discard. `applyDrag` dispatches on `offset.kind`, taking the parent's resolved position (`anchor`, for polar/cartesian) and the DRAGGED NODE's OWN previous resolved position (`previousPosition`, for `formula` — its `x`/`y` are the absolute position directly per frame.ts, never anchor-relative, a distinction the first draft of this function got wrong and a test now pins).

**Why the canvas itself is untouched.** `OverlayCanvas.tsx`'s pointer handlers currently do exactly two things — pan the viewport, or fire a click-select — and nothing in this environment can render `App.tsx`/`ToolsPane.tsx` to exercise a THIRD pointer mode (drag-to-move-a-shape) against a real canvas, real `PointerEvent`s, and real coordinate math. This repo has twice already found a class of defect — legibility, not correctness — that survives every review round and shows up only on the first real read (the checker, the formatter); wiring untestable interaction code into a shared component on top of an already-large session was judged the wrong place to add a THIRD instance of that risk. The math this entry closes is what a future session needs to wire; nothing about it should need to be re-derived.

**Verification.** `npm run typecheck`, `npm run lint` (0 errors repo-wide; the same pre-existing `react-refresh/only-export-components` warnings every context-provider file in this tree already carries), `npm run validate:reference`, `npm run check:generated-types` all clean. **2026-09-01 — Newcomer tutorial follow-up: multi-region spotlighting, an "Add them for me" shortcut, stricter attribute completion on three steps, and one stale command name traced to a real design/implementation drift.**

Ash reported five usability gaps in Tutorial A after using it: several steps only highlighted one of two things the copy told the user to interact with, three completion checks let the step finish the moment a bare command existed (before any of the attributes the body asked for), the satisfied-tick pause felt too quick to register, and the per-player-resources step ("Everyone else's resources") was four near-identical hand-typed commands with nothing teaching that repetition.

**1. Multi-region spotlighting (`extraAnchors`).** `TutorialStep` gained `extraAnchors?: Anchor[]` (`types.ts`) — `anchor` still positions the callout, `extraAnchors` adds more cutouts to the same spotlight. This forced `TutorialOverlay.tsx`'s dimming to change shape: rev 1's four-div "everything but the rect" band system cannot compose across more than one disjoint rect (two independent band sets double-dim the shared background, and a pixel inside spotlight A is still covered by spotlight B's own "everything but B" bands) — replaced with one `<svg>` holding a `<mask>` (one white full-viewport rect, one black rect per spotlighted region) painted through a single dim-coloured rect, which composes correctly for any N ≥ 1. Applied to: "Random or direct placement" (Player Setup tab + Add command button — the step it was reported against), "Hills"/"Cliffs"/"Trees"/"A road to the hill"/"Starting units" (their section tab + `breakdown.cardList`, so the Add-command control introduced by [the prior session's `breakdown.cardList` widening] stays in frame on every step that asks for a new command, not just the three that already anchored there directly), and "This is what it really is" (the Code tab + a new `code.editor` container anchor on `CodePane.tsx`'s `div.editorFrame`).

**2. Stricter completion on three steps.** "Hills," "Trees," and "A road to the hill" all completed the instant their command existed, before any attribute the step's own body asked for. "Hills" now requires `base_terrain`/`number_of_clumps`/`number_of_tiles` on `create_elevation` (was bare `hasCommand`). "Trees" now requires all four of `base_terrain`/`land_percent`/`number_of_clumps`/`set_avoid_player_start_areas` on `create_terrain` (was `base_terrain` alone — already an attribute check, just satisfied by the first attribute added regardless of the other three). "A road to the hill" now requires the command AND two distinct `replace_terrain` attributes matching `GRASS ROAD` / `DIRT ROAD` respectively (`scriptChecks.ts` gained no new helper — `hasCommandWithAttributeWhere` already existed and covers a same-named-attribute-twice-with-different-args check that `hasCommandWithAttribute` alone cannot, since it only tests attribute-name presence).

**A real bug found while touching that third check, not introduced by it.** The connection step's own command name has been split three ways since rev 1: the design doc's Sec.9.1 table and the test fixture (`fixtures/goldenHill.rms`) both said `create_connect_all_players_land`, but the SHIPPED `content/rmsBasics.ts` already said `create_connect_to_nonplayer_land` — a silent deviation from the doc that happened to be the correct one and was never reconciled, which is exactly why `road-to-hill`'s check has been failing against the fixture (visible in `rmsBasics.test.ts`) since the tutorial shipped. The guide settles which is right: `create_connect_all_players_land` "Connections will be generated between the origins of all player lands... Connections may pass through neutral lands if the cost is favorable" (guide:1757-1760) — opportunistic at best, no guarantee of ever reaching the hill the step is titled after — while `create_connect_to_nonplayer_land` is documented to "Connect all player lands to all neutral lands" (guide:1858-1861), which is the step's actual goal. Fixed the fixture and the design doc to match the (correct) implementation rather than the other way around, and updated the two test files that had hardcoded the stale name (`scriptChecks.test.ts`, `rmsBasics.test.ts`).

**3. Auto-advance pause lengthened.** `AUTO_ADVANCE_DELAY_MS` 600ms → 1100ms (`TutorialOverlay.tsx`) — 600ms read as too quick to actually see the tick before the callout moved on.

**4. "Add them for me" on "Everyone else's resources."** New `TutorialStep.autoFill?: { label; buildEdit(ctx) => StepTextEdit | null }` — an extra button beside Next that performs the step's own instructions rather than teaching a new mechanism. Deliberately bypasses the Breakdown patch engine's node-anchored intents (`addCommand`/`addAttribute`): those need the newly-created node handed back before the next attribute can target it, which isn't available synchronously outside a React re-render, so chaining four commands' worth from outside the Breakdown UI would need either a fragile intermediate-reparse loop or a new batch `EditIntent` widening the property-tested patch engine's surface for a one-off tutorial shortcut. New `src/tutorial/autoFill.ts`'s `appendObjectBlocks` builds one text edit directly from the live `ParseResult` instead — same anchor rule `computeEdit.ts`'s `insertIntoSection` uses (last item of the section's last concrete `SectionNode`), same indent/EOL detection (`formatStyle.ts`'s `detectEol`/`detectIndentStep`/`lineIndentOf`, already exported and reused rather than duplicated), for a whole batch in one edit. `App.tsx` threads `doc.applyTextEdits` down to `TutorialOverlay` (same function CodePane/Advanced Tools already push edits through — one `pushEditOperations` call, one undo entry) for exactly this. The four commands inserted are the same FORAGE_BUSH/GOLD/STONE/OAKTREE blocks (with the same attribute values) already in `fixtures/goldenHill.rms`, so the shortcut and the "correct answer" the completion check is written against can never drift apart.

**Verification.** `npm run typecheck`, `npm run lint` (0 errors; all warnings pre-existing), `npm run validate:reference` (the new `tutorial.autoFill` `ui-help.json` entry validates), and `npm run check:generated-types` all clean. `src/tutorial/` suite: 61/61 passing (`registry.test.ts` extended to check `extraAnchors` too, for all three of its existing anchor-validity assertions). Full `npm test`: **100 files / 2538 tests**, comfortably above the floor (68/1638) with no floor bump needed — this session edited existing test files' assertions rather than adding new ones. Not verified: the app has never been run outside the real Tauri host (standing environment limitation, CLAUDE.md), so the spotlight's actual on-screen appearance with two simultaneous cutouts, and the auto-fill button's real click-through, are unverified by anything but the automated suite and reading the code.

**Same-day follow-up: a third `extraAnchors` region for "Random or direct placement."** Ash asked for the whole Breakdown pane to stay undimmed on this step too, not just the Player Setup tab and the Add command button. New container anchor `breakdown.pane` on `BreakdownPane.tsx`'s root `div.pane` (the whole tab — side panel, section tabs and card list together, same "root of the thing" pattern `sidePanel.preview` already uses for its own whole-pane step). Added as a third entry in the step's `extraAnchors` array rather than replacing the other two — the tab and button still get their own tighter rings so the copy's "press + Add command" instruction still points at something precise, while the mask's third hole keeps the rest of the editing surface visible. `npm run typecheck`/`lint`/`src/tutorial` suite (61/61) all clean; no test changes needed since `registry.test.ts`'s anchor-existence checks already walk every step's `extraAnchors` generically.

**Same-day, second follow-up: `breakdown.pane` → `breakdown.main` (excludes the preview pane), plus a manual callout nudge.** Ash caught that `breakdown.pane` undimmed `MapSidePanel` too, which he didn't want — the anchor moved from `BreakdownPane.tsx`'s `div.pane` (the whole tab) to `div.main` (tabs + card list only, `MapSidePanel` is `.main`'s sibling, not its child) and was renamed to match what it now actually covers. Separately: this step's callout, positioned beside the Player Setup tab, was landing on top of where CommandPicker's dropdown opens once the user presses + Add command — a different control than the anchor being pointed at, so the existing beside/below/above placement algorithm has no way to see it coming. Rather than special-case this one step inside the placement algorithm, `TutorialStep` gained two generic escape hatches: `calloutNudge?: { x?; y? }` (added to the computed position, clamped to the same viewport margins as everything else — `TutorialOverlay.tsx`'s `place()` now runs every anchored branch's result through an `applyNudge` helper before calling `setPosition`) and `calloutMaxWidthPx?: number` (an inline `maxWidth` override, since inline style beats `TutorialOverlay.module.css`'s `.callout` class). This step sets `calloutNudge: { x: 368 }` and `calloutMaxWidthPx: 380` — 368 is `CommandPicker.module.css`'s `.panel { width: 22rem }` (352px at the default 16px root, no root font-size override anywhere in `src/`) plus a small gap, not a guessed number. `npm run typecheck`/`lint`/`src/tutorial` suite (61/61) clean.

**Same-day, third follow-up: the same nudge for steps 1 and 4, a real mount-timing bug behind "the Code step doesn't highlight Monaco," and the big one — every value-naming completion check was satisfied by a placeholder, not the value.** Three separate reports, one session.

**1. Nudge/scope parity for "Start a new script" and "Give the players some land."** "Give the players some land" (`player-lands`) gained the identical treatment as "Random or direct placement" — `extraAnchors: [{region: breakdown.main}]`, `calloutNudge: {x: 368}`, `calloutMaxWidthPx: 380` — because its own anchor (the Add command button) spans the full width of the card area exactly the way "Random or direct placement"'s did, so CommandPicker's dropdown opens in the same place the default callout position would land. "Start a new script" (`start-new-file`) got `calloutNudge: {x: 300}` for a different dropdown — the File menu, which opens directly below the File button at the far left of the title bar, and the callout's default beside-the-anchor position landed on top of it. Named honestly in both the content file and the design doc: `TitleBar.module.css`'s `.dropdown` has no single fixed-width CSS literal to derive an exact clearance from the way `CommandPicker.module.css`'s `.panel` does (`min-width: 170px`, actual width driven by "Save As…" plus its hotkey hint) — 300px is a generous estimate, not a measured figure, and is called out as such rather than dressed up as precision.

**2. "The Code step should highlight Monaco too — right now it does not" was a real bug, not a missing feature.** The `code.editor` anchor and its wiring into the "This is what it really is" step (both landed in the prior session) were correct; they just never fired. `TutorialOverlay`'s spotlight is computed once per step in a `useLayoutEffect`, plus continuously via a `requestAnimationFrame` loop — but that loop is gated to `check` steps only (`step?.completion.kind === "check" && !satisfied`), and "This is what it really is" is `manual`. A step's `navigate.tab` is applied by `TutorialContext`'s own PASSIVE `useEffect`, which fires AFTER `TutorialOverlay`'s LAYOUT effect in the same commit that makes the step active — so the very first (and, for a manual step, ONLY) `place()` call ran before `navigate.tab` had switched to Code, before `CodePane` (and `code.editor`) existed in the DOM. `document.querySelector` found nothing, and nothing ever asked again. Fixed by adding `activeTab` to the placement effect's dependency array — not because `place()` reads it, but purely to force a re-run once the tab (and its DOM) actually changes, a render later. Generalizes beyond this one step: any future manual step whose anchor lives in a tab reached via `navigate.tab` would have hit the identical race.

**3. The bigger one: every completion check that named a specific value was satisfied by whatever `computeEdit` fills a fresh slot with, not the value the step asked for.** `renderCommand`/`renderAttribute` both route through `formatStyle.ts`'s `renderNamed`, which has ALWAYS filled every argument with `placeholderFor(def)` — `default ?? min ?? 0` for a numeric type — the instant a command or attribute is created, whether from CommandPicker or an attribute row's `+`. A presence-only check (`hasCommand`/`hasCommandWithAttribute`/`hasObjectWith`) is satisfied by that placeholder before the user retypes anything, and with the auto-advance timer running on a `check` step (1100ms as of the very first same-day follow-up above), that is genuinely under a second in practice — exactly what Ash reported. This was already half-fixed in the prior session (the elevation/terrain/connection steps got attribute-NAME checks instead of bare `hasCommand`), but a name check has the identical hole one level down: the attribute exists with the WRONG value. Queried every numeric argument this tutorial's completion checks touch against its `language.json` definition to find which placeholders actually collide with the desired value (none of this was guessed): `circle_radius` (no default, falls back to `min` `-50`, wants `35`), `base_elevation` (default `0`, wants `3`), `land_id` (no default, falls back to `min` `-10`, wants `10`), `number_of_clumps` (default `1`, wants `10` then `20` in two different steps), `number_of_tiles` (no default, falls back to `0`, wants `600`), `land_percent` (default `100`, wants `10`), `set_avoid_player_start_areas` (no default, falls back to `0`, wants `8`), `place_on_specific_land_id` (no default, falls back to `0`, wants `10`), and the two cliff commands' own positional counts (`min_number_of_cliffs` default `3` — coincidentally already right — `max_number_of_cliffs` default `8`, wants `6`). Only `base_terrain`/`terrain_type` (default `GRASS`, matching every step that asks for it) were never actually at risk. Two new `scriptChecks.ts` helpers close the gap the existing `hasCommandWithAttributeWhere` couldn't reach on its own: `hasCommandWhere` (a predicate over a COMMAND's own positional arguments — needed for the two standalone cliff commands, which aren't attributes of anything) and `hasObjectWithAttributeWhere` (`hasObjectWith` plus a value predicate — needed for `place_on_specific_land_id`). Six steps' completion checks were rewritten against these (`player-lands`, `hill-in-the-middle`, `hills`, `cliffs`, `trees`, `gold-on-the-hill`); `road-to-hill` already used a value predicate from the prior session's connection-command fix.

**A second real fixture bug found while re-deriving the exact values.** `fixtures/goldenHill.rms`'s `create_terrain FOREST` block had `number_of_clumps 12`, while the step's own body text does the arithmetic "10/20 = 0.5 land percent per group" — internally consistent at 20, not 12. Nobody had ever needed the fixture's number_of_clumps to be exactly right before (the OLD check just verified the name existed), so the drift was invisible; the new value check would have failed the fixture itself had this not been caught, which is exactly the kind of thing `rmsBasics.test.ts`'s "every check step is satisfied by the finished script" assertion exists to catch — and did, on the first local run. Fixture corrected to `20`.

**Verification.** `npm run typecheck`, `npm run lint` (0 errors, only pre-existing warnings), `npm run validate:reference` all clean. `src/tutorial/` suite grew from 61 to **63** (two new `scriptChecks.test.ts` assertions covering the new helpers, both fixture-driven and null-parse negative cases) — all passing, including `rmsBasics.test.ts`'s full round-trip against the corrected fixture. Full `npm test`: **100 files / 2540 tests**, floor 68/1638, comfortably clear. Not verified: real click-through timing in the running app (the 1100ms window actually feeling sufficient once typing a real value is what's being waited on, rather than a placeholder) — same standing Tauri-host limitation as every other UI slice in this file.

**Same-day, fourth follow-up: "same place as the previous step," and the value-check sweep continues into the three sections it hadn't reached yet.** Ash's own use of the tutorial found four more gaps, all the same two shapes as the ones already fixed this session.

**1. "A hill in the middle" pinned to "Give the players some land"'s exact position, and its own missing value check.** Rather than compute a nudge that happens to land in the same place, `hill-in-the-middle`'s anchor changed from `region:breakdown.cardList` to the SAME configuration as `player-lands` — `help:breakdown.addCommand` + `extraAnchors: [region:breakdown.main]` + `calloutNudge: {x:368}` + `calloutMaxWidthPx:380` — literally the same DOM element and the same arithmetic, so the callout is guaranteed to land in the same spot rather than merely a similar one; two steps that both read as "add a command here" should not relocate the tutorial window between them. Gold on the hill and Everyone else's resources moved right, and Gold on the hill's remaining values checked.** Both steps' Add-command press opens the identical CommandPicker dropdown at the identical position as the LAND_GENERATION steps (same full-width button, same section-relative layout), so both gained the identical `calloutNudge: {x:368}` / `calloutMaxWidthPx: 380` — WITHOUT changing their existing `region:breakdown.cardList` anchor, unlike `hill-in-the-middle` above: these two weren't asked to match another step's position exactly, just to move by "a similar distance," so the minimal change (nudge only, same anchor) was the right scope rather than restructuring what gets highlighted. "Gold on the hill" also gained checks for `number_of_objects` (`8`), `number_of_groups` (`4`) and `set_gaia_object_only`'s presence — previously only `place_on_specific_land_id` was checked, and the fixture already carried the right values for all three so no fixture change was needed there. **Verification.** `npm run typecheck`, `npm run lint` (0 errors, only pre-existing warnings), `npm run validate:reference` all clean. `src/tutorial/` suite: 63/63 passing (no new test count — existing `rmsBasics.test.ts`/`scriptChecks.test.ts` assertions already exercise every step against the corrected fixture). Full `npm test`: **100 files / 2540 tests**, floor 68/1638. Not verified: the visual claim that `hill-in-the-middle`'s callout now lands pixel-identical to `player-lands`' — guaranteed by construction (same anchor element, same arithmetic) but not seen on screen, same standing Tauri-host limitation as everything else in this file.

**Same-day, fifth follow-up: an explicit audit swept every remaining step's completion check against its own body text for un-verified values, prompted by one concrete miss (`create_player_lands` never checked `land_percent`).** The four prior value-check passes this session (rows 3/4/6/7/8/10/11 of Sec.9.1) each fixed the specific gap reported, but none of them was a systematic pass over EVERY step — this one was, checking every attribute AND every command's own positional argument named in each step's body against what its `completion.test` actually verifies.

**Four more gaps found, all the same two shapes already established this session.** (1) `player-lands` (row 3) checked only `circle_radius` — the LAST of the three attributes its body lists (`terrain_type`, `land_percent`, `circle_radius`) — a "check the final one" shorthand that rows 6 and 8 had also used before their own gaps were found. (2) `hill-in-the-middle` (row 4) was missing `land_percent` (`8`, default `100`) and `land_position` (`50`/`50`, no default, falls back to its shared `min` `0`/`0`) — two of the body's five named attributes, added the same session `terrain_type` was but somehow still gapped. (3) `hills` (row 6) and (4) `trees` (row 8) had each checked every ATTRIBUTE their body names but never the COMMAND's own positional argument — `create_elevation`'s height (`4`, declared default `0`) and `create_terrain`'s terrain constant (`FOREST`, no default, falls back to the literal string `"TODO"`) respectively. Both use the new-this-session `hasCommandWhere`, same as Cliffs' standalone commands. All four fixes needed no fixture changes — every value was already correct in `fixtures/goldenHill.rms`, confirmed by this round's full `rmsBasics.test.ts` pass; only the CHECKS were missing.

**The durable lesson, recorded in `tutorial-design.md`'s Sec.8 alongside the rest of this session's placeholder-timing notes**: "checked every attribute" and "checked everything the body names a value for" are not the same claim — a command's own arguments are a second, easy-to-forget category, and three separate passes (add `*Where` to whatever's already checked → check every attribute → check every command argument too) were needed to actually close this class of gap for good. Cliffs (row 7) and Starting units (row 10) were already complete by the time this audit ran, from the immediately preceding round.
