Full `npm test`: **100 files / 2540 tests**, floor 68/1638.

**Same-day, sixth follow-up: Tutorial B ("Tour of Age of RMS" / "New to Age of RMS") could run from a clean install with every anchor past the first permanently unresolvable, because nothing ever asked for a file.** Ash: "the new to AoRMS needs a script opened to properly show the functionality, but the tutorial doesn't make the user do this."

Rev 1's own header comment reasoned "runs against whatever the user already has open, including nothing… unlike Tutorial A it asks for no file, so it never needs a step 0" — and conflated two separate claims. Not requiring a NEW, EMPTY file is correct: this tour never edits the document, so any existing map serves fine. But "including nothing" is not: `BreakdownPane` renders a bare `PlaceholderPane` instead of its real layout whenever `hasFile === false`, so `MapSidePanel` (`sidePanel.preview`/`sidePanel.reference`), the preview toggle, the notes drawer and the resource totals don't exist in the DOM at all with nothing open. Starting this tour fresh — the exact path a brand-new user takes from the welcome pane — left six of its eight steps pointing at anchors that would never resolve for the whole run, since neither this tour nor anything else in the app ever opens a file on the user's behalf.

**Fix: a new first step, "Open a map to explore"** (`content/appTour.ts`) — `check`, `test: (ctx) => ctx.hasFile`, anchored on `help:titleBar.file` with the same `calloutNudge: {x:300}` as Tutorial A's own step 0 (identical File-dropdown-clearance reasoning, cross-referenced in the comment rather than restated). Body nudges toward opening an EXISTING map ("the best way to see real numbers") while still accepting `File ▸ New` for someone with nothing handy — the check can't tell a populated map from an empty one, and demanding a specific kind of file would be asking more of a three-minute tour than it needs. Every step after it keeps Sec.10's original constraint (no step may assert what's on screen — a map, a reference-table mode, a resource total can all look different from what the tour author saw); the gate only guarantees the SURFACE exists to look at, not what's on it. Tutorial B is now 9 steps, not 8.

**New test file** `src/tutorial/__tests__/appTour.test.ts` (3 tests) — the gate step is false with no file and true with one, it's step index 0, and every step after it is still `manual` (nothing else in this tour should ever grow a check, per Sec.10's own "tour, not an exercise" rule — a mutation-style guard against that drifting unnoticed). `registry.test.ts` already covered title-length/anchor-existence/unique-id for this tutorial generically and needed no changes.

**Verification.** `npm run typecheck`, `npm run lint` (0 errors, only pre-existing warnings). `src/tutorial/` suite: **66/66** (up from 63 — one new file, 3 tests). Full `npm test`: **101 files / 2543 tests**, floor 68/1638. Not verified: the real welcome-pane → "Tour of Age of RMS" → clean-install path in the running app — same standing Tauri-host limitation as every other UI slice in this file, though this is exactly the path the bug report describes, so it is the highest-value manual check owed from this session.

**Same-day, seventh follow-up: the new step-1 File dropdown was rendering dimmed underneath the tutorial's own spotlight, a plain z-index gap the previous fix never had reason to check.** Ash: on Tutorial A's step 1 (and, since it shares the same component, Tutorial B's new step 1 too), opening the File menu shows the dropdown looking dimmed rather than sitting in front of the tutorial's dim layer.

Root cause: `TitleBar.module.css`'s `.dropdown` was `z-index: 10`, while `TutorialOverlay.module.css`'s dim SVG and ring are `900`/`901`. Both are portalled/positioned against the same page-level stacking context (the overlay via `createPortal` into `document.body`, the dropdown via `position: absolute` inside `TitleBar`, itself a normal, non-transformed child of that same body), so the dim layer painted straight over the dropdown wherever they overlapped — the dim layer's own `pointer-events: none` kept it clickable underneath, but visually it read as covered. This is NOT the same shape as the mount-timing bug fixed two follow-ups ago (that was about the spotlight HOLE not existing yet); here the hole is irrelevant, because the spotlight only ever covers the File BUTTON (the step's own anchor) and was never meant to extend down to a dropdown that only exists once the button is clicked — no geometry fix could have closed this, only stacking order could.

**Fix: `TitleBar.module.css`'s `.dropdown` raised to `z-index: 910`** — above the dim layer and ring (900/901). That also puts it above the callout itself (902), which is fine rather than fixed-on-purpose: the tutorial already nudges its own callout clear of this dropdown's footprint (`calloutNudge`), so the two are not expected to overlap on screen regardless of which would win. Fixes both of `TitleBar.tsx`'s dropdowns (File and Help share the one `.dropdown` class), and therefore both tutorials' step-1 for free, since it's the same component either way.

**One related latent instance fixed preventively, not reported broken.** `CommandPicker.module.css`'s `.panel` had the identical shape of gap (`z-index: 20`, comfortably below the dim layer) — currently masked by coincidence, since every tutorial step that can open this picker (`random-or-direct`/`player-lands`/`hill-in-the-middle`/`gold-on-the-hill`/`everyone-elses-resources`) spotlights a region (`breakdown.main`/`breakdown.cardList`) wide enough to contain wherever the picker renders. That coincidence is exactly the kind of thing a future narrower spotlight would silently break, the same way the File dropdown's did. Raised to `z-index: 920` for the same reason, at zero behavioural cost outside a running tutorial (nothing else in the app's z-index range 20-899 needs to sit above or below it any differently — full inventory: `SectionView`'s sticky header `1`, `ReferenceTable` `1`, `HelpTip`/`DiagnosticTooltip` popups `100`, `dialog.module.css` modals `1000`, `UnsavedChangesDialog` `1100`, both comfortably clear of the new `910`/`920`).

**Verification.** `npm run typecheck`, `npm run lint` (0 errors, only pre-existing warnings), `src/tutorial/` suite (66/66) — a pure z-index change touches no logic, so no test changes were needed or expected. Not verified: the actual on-screen appearance (same standing Tauri-host limitation as everything else in this file) — this is a CSS stacking fix, and stacking order is exactly the kind of thing that's cheap to get wrong in a way tests can't see; Ash's own visual confirmation is the real check owed here.

**2026-09-02 (later) — Post-slice-5 review: two silent-discard defects in the new drag path fixed, and the shape-kind gap written up as its own escalation.**

A read of the slice-5 continuation's own code, not of its build-log entry. Three findings were acted on, two as fixes and one as a document; two more were named and left. Nothing here changes what slice 5 built, only what it does at two edges the first cut did not reach.

**1. `applyDrag` silently discarded a live symbolic reference on `polar` and `cartesian` offsets.** Sec.7.3's invertibility rule was implemented for the `formula` offset kind only, and the other two arms simply overwrote whatever was there with `num(...)` literals. Two shapes reach that code carrying a reference that means something. A group member's own theta is `add(group.rotation, offsetTerm)` (`expand.ts`), so a ring whose ROTATION is symbolic (Sec.4.5's own worked `ROTATION_PLAYER` example) gives every member a theta that steers off that parameter, and one drag froze that one member at a single angle while its siblings kept rotating per seed. And any placement whose radius/angle/dx/dy was typed as a formula, which the panel's own `FormulaField` has allowed since the formula field landed the day before, hit the same path. **The second case is what makes this a live defect rather than a latent one: the field that makes a symbolic offset typeable and the drag that overwrites it shipped one day apart, in the same slice.** Both arms now decline with a stated reason, which is Sec.7.3's own prescribed behaviour ("the handle is a read-only marker and the panel says why") and matches what `reExpand` already does one layer over, where a non-numeric member offset is left untouched rather than rewritten.

The predicate is `evalClosed`, promoted out of `reExpand.ts`'s own private copy into `compiler/expr.ts` so the merge rule and the drag guard cannot drift apart on the same question. **It is deliberately not `isFullyNumericLiteral`**, which sits beside it and would have been the obvious choice: `add` never folds (`expr.ts:24` builds a `bin` unconditionally), so EVERY group member's theta is a `bin` even when the rotation is a plain number, and a literal-shape test would have refused every ordinary ring member. A test pins that case directly.

**A second site had the same defect and does not go through `applyDrag` at all.** `handleGizmoDrag` patches a `ShapeGroup`'s own radius/rotation, so a group whose rotation is a formula would have had it replaced by one drag of the rotation handle, taking every member's steering with it. It now declines in the same words, through an exported `symbolicDeclineReason`, so the two refusals cannot diverge into two phrasings of one rule. The handles still draw; Sec.7.3's read-only-marker state is exactly "visible, refuses, says why".

**Mutation-tested**: `symbolicComponents` hardcoded to return `[]`, confirmed three decline tests red, restored.

**2. The rim gesture won over the body gesture unconditionally, on every land at once.** `hitTestDragStart` tested the rim before the body and over all circles, so a press inside land A that fell near land B's edge started a chain from B rather than moving A, and on a map with several lands no press reliably meant "move this one". Worse for small lands: at a ~1.8-tile band a 3.6-tile land is rim over 75% of its own area, so the move gesture was unreachable on exactly the aux lands Bulls_Eyes is made of. Two changes. The rim is now scoped to the SELECTED land, on the reading that Sec.7.3 calls it a rim HANDLE and a handle belongs to the selection, which is the rule the two gizmo handles already follow. And `hitTestRim` caps the band per circle at 35% of that circle's own radius, so the inner ~65% of every land stays a body drag however small the land is. The cap lives inside the geometry function rather than at the call site that knows about small lands, per this file's own rule about where an exception belongs.

**The first version of that test was not a test, and only the mutant said so.** Written the natural way, asserting the centre and the edge, it passed identically with and without the cap: at rTiles 3 against a 1.8 band the centre is already outside the rim in both worlds. Rewritten against the one radius where the capped and uncapped bands actually disagree (2.4 tiles out on a 4-tile land, 1.6 from the rim, inside the uncapped band and outside the capped one), and mutation-tested twice rather than once, since the cap can be wrong in two directions: with the cap deleted, and with the cap REPLACING the requested thickness instead of bounding it. Each mutant now kills exactly one test and it is that test's own. Same lesson as BUG-005 piece 2's three surviving mutants, arriving on a fixture chosen for readability.

**3. Item 6's shape kinds, written up rather than left as a paragraph in an entry.** `docs/land-placement-shape-kinds-escalation.md` is new, with a pointer from `land-placement-design.md` Sec.12 as **Q9** so it is reachable from the authoritative document rather than only from here. It splits the cut item into the three questions it actually is: what each kind's geometry is (and that `polygon` needs a vertex count and `arc` a sweep angle, neither of which exists on `ShapeGroup`); whether the kinds stay `polar`, which they must, because a perimeter distribution emits `cartesian` members and `reExpand`'s delta branch detaches every non-`polar` member, so a square's members would silently go `positionDetached` on the first repeat-count edit; and whose slice it is. **The recommendation is to narrow the type to `circle` rather than build six geometries**, on the same reasoning Sec.6.4 used to defer the importer: the three corpus scripts carrying this idiom are all rings and chains, no measurement has ever been pointed at the polygonal kinds, and Sec.1's own "circle, square, triangle, ..." is a wishlist sentence written before the model existed. `model.ts`'s `radius` comment says "circumradius", the word for a polygon's vertex distance, which is the only evidence anywhere of what was intended and is a hint rather than a decision.

**One decision deliberately not taken, and filed in that same note.** Declining a symbolic drag is the conservative half of Sec.7.3's rule. The better behaviour is to ABSORB the delta into the numeric term the way `tryInvertFormulaCoordinate` already does for a reference plus a constant, since a member's theta is exactly that shape, which would let the member move where it was dropped AND keep following its group's rotation. That is a decision about what a drag means rather than a bug fix, so it is written down in section 6 of the escalation note instead of improvised here.

**Two findings named and left**, both real and neither acted on. `useEmission`'s header cites Sec.3.4's 0.173 ms as the reason re-running on every edit is not a performance concern, and that figure is `emitAlpModel`'s const-table evaluation only; the hook also runs `buildLanguageIndex` and `instantiateScript` over the whole document, and `model` is in its dependency list, so what used to fire on a keystroke in a form field now fires on every pointermove, with `computeApplyEdits` recomputing on each resulting render. **The measurement is scoped to a different operation and to a rate two orders of magnitude lower**, which is this file's own "a measurement pins the property its arms varied" rule landing on a doc comment. One probe timing the other two calls settles it, and it is worth having before the run sheet, since a laggy drag will otherwise be filed as a rendering problem. Separately, `pointercancel` during a shape drag delivers nothing and returns, but the `move` phase has already written to the model, so a cancelled drag commits its last position; the original handler took care to distinguish `clicked === false` and the new arm inherits the flag without using it. The root cause is that there is no gesture-start snapshot, which also forecloses an Escape-to-cancel later.

**Verification.** `npm run typecheck` clean, `npm run lint` 0 errors (the same two pre-existing `react-refresh/only-export-components` warnings on `landPlacementModel.tsx`/`panelPreviewSeed.tsx` every prior slice has carried). Full `npm test`: **106 files / 2589 tests, 146.28 s, floor 68/1651**, which is 2583 + 6 exactly, no new files and no parallel-session drift in this row, the +6 being four `dragMath.test.ts` assertions and two rewritten in `rimHitTest.test.ts`. `reExpand.test.ts` green and unmodified across the `evalClosed` extraction, which is the regression test for that move.

**Still open, unchanged by this pass.** R0 (4b's twelve-step run sheet) and slice 5's own ten-step sheet, neither ever run. The `useEmission` call-rate probe and the `pointercancel` commit, both named above. `RandomParam`-from-formula. Live invalid-drop-target feedback on the rim drag. Q9's own three questions. The importer.

**2026-09-02 (later still) — First manual run of the Land Placement panel, on Bulls_Eyes.rms. Four reported defects, one cause. A real P4 defect measured. Tool Explanation dialog built.**

The panel had never been run. Every slice from 4b onward carried a run sheet nobody had executed, and this entry is the first observation of the built thing rather than of its code. Six questions were put to it; five are behaviour and the sixth asked for a feature. **Four of the five behaviour answers are one root cause, and it is a design decision working exactly as written.**

**Bulls_Eyes.rms has no ALP fence, so the panel loaded `EMPTY_MODEL`, and every interactive surface in the tool keys off the model.** `readFenceModel` returns null on a script the tool did not write, which Sec.6.1 and Sec.10.4 #3 fix deliberately as no partial adopt. From there the chain is mechanical and each link was reported as its own bug. The tree renders "No lands yet" because `flattenPlacementTree` is given no placements. The canvas draws no circles because `buildOverlayShapes` reads `emission.quantities`, which is empty. `onTileClick` calls `hitTestCircles` against an empty array and gets null, so clicking a land does nothing. And `hitTestDragStart` returns null for the same reason, at which point `OverlayCanvas.onPointerDown` takes its `mode: "pan"` branch, so dragging a land pans the map. **The one observation that identifies the cause is that re-rolling moved the lands**: only the base layer, a real generation of the document at the panel seed, can do that, so what was on screen was the script's own output and never the tool's overlay.

Nothing here is a fault in the drag path, the hit tests or the tree. They were exercised for the first time against a model that was empty by design, and the tool reported that state with a four-word sentence in a corner of the right column while the canvas showed a map covered in lands. **The gap is that the panel never says which lands it owns.**

**The preconditions strip carries a real defect, and it is the one thing in this round that is wrong rather than unexplained.** The strip listed roughly 145 names under "These names would collide with existing script symbols", every one of them a constant the script itself defines. Measured with a throwaway probe against Bulls_Eyes at playerCount 2, seed 12345: model empty, `emission.ok` true, `scriptSymbols` 133, `emission.resolved` **133**, P4 collisions **133**, and collisions that are NOT the document's own symbols **0**. The first eight reproduce the reported list in order.

The cause is a field answering a different question from the one its consumer asks. `verify.ts:66` builds `resolved` as `new Map(scriptSymbols)` and then adds the emitted cells, which is correct and load-bearing, since a cell's own expression has to resolve against the document's constants. `LandPlacementPanel.tsx:121` then passes `[...emission.resolved.keys()]` as P4's CANDIDATE names. So the panel hands P4 the document's symbols and asks whether they collide with a reserved set built from the document's symbols, and the answer is yes, for all of them, on every script that defines a constant. An empty model makes it total; a non-empty one buries the real candidates in the same list. **`checkP4ForPanel` and `reservedNamesForApply` are both correct and were both written to avoid a self-collision one layer up; the defect is entirely in what the call site passes.** The fix is for `EmissionOk` to carry its own emitted names rather than have the panel infer them by keying off a map that was deliberately seeded with something else, which is the same shape as `useEmission`'s own header comment warning that `resolved` and `scriptSymbols` answer different questions. Not fixed this pass, by instruction.

**The seed observation is by design and the design blocks the comparison it was asked for.** The two previews disagree because `usePanelPreviewSeed` draws from `Math.random()` independently of the document's seed, which Sec.3.3 fixes and which is right, since the panel's seed must survive a tab switch and must not write back to `PreviewViewContext`. There is no control anywhere that sets one to the other, so "switch to Breakdown at the same seed and compare one land by eye" cannot be carried out today. Worth a Match document seed action beside Re-roll before the next run sheet, since eyeball agreement between the vector tier and the full tier is the check the canvas exists to make possible.

**Built: the Tool Explanation button and dialog.** `LandPlacementHelpDialog.tsx` and its module CSS are new, opened from a button pinned to the right end of the +Role/+Ring/+Land row and dismissed by Escape, the backdrop or its own Close button, following `UnsavedChangesDialog`/`SettingsDialog` and reusing `dialog.module.css` for the chrome. It documents what the tool writes, the fence rule that produced four of this round's five answers, the role-first build order, parents and frames, every canvas gesture, the panel-owned seed, and the warning strip.

**One implementation note worth keeping.** The auto margin that pins the button right sits on a span wrapping the `HelpTip`, not on the button. `HelpTip` renders its own `display: inline-block` wrapper, so the button is not a child of the flex row and `margin-left: auto` on it resolves against the wrapper and does nothing. Any future right-aligned control in a HelpTip-wrapped toolbar has the same trap.

**Verification.** `npm run typecheck` clean. `npm run lint` clean on all three changed files. `npm run validate:reference` passes with the two new `ui-help.json` entries (`landPlacement.explain`, `landPlacement.explainClose`), and the file round-trips byte-identical to its own canonical form, so no formatting churn was introduced. `helpCoverage.test.ts` gains a case naming the new dialog file, since its `HelpTip` lives one import away from the only file that suite scanned: **8 tests, up from 7**, and **mutation-tested**, with the dialog's `explainClose` id misspelled the gate goes red naming the exact id, and the file was restored from a byte copy rather than by reverse substitution. **The panel itself is still unverified outside the Tauri host**, which is the standing environment constraint, so the dialog's layout and the button's position are owed one `npm run tauri dev` pass.

**Still open, and this round adds to it.** The P4 candidate-names defect above. A Match document seed control. Some way for the panel to say that the lands on screen are not its own. Everything the previous entry lists as open is untouched.

**2026-09-02 (later still, second pass) — The P4 candidate-names defect fixed, and the call site given no way to be wrong again.**

Reported from the first manual run (entry above). The preconditions strip told a user that ~145 names would collide with existing script symbols, every one of them a constant that user's own script defines, on a model with nothing in it.

**The comparison was never wrong.** `checkP4ForPanel` and `reservedNamesForApply` both did exactly what they were written to do. `verify.ts:66` builds `resolved` as `new Map(scriptSymbols)` before walking the emitted cells, which is correct and load-bearing, since a cell's own expression has to resolve against the constants the document already defines. The panel then passed `[...emission.resolved.keys()]` as P4's CANDIDATE names, so P4 was asked whether the script's constants collide with a reserved set built from the script's constants. Measured on Bulls_Eyes at 2 players: `scriptSymbols` 133, `resolved` 133, collisions **133**, collisions not from the document's own symbols **0**.

**Two changes, and the second is the one that matters.** `EmissionOk` gains `emittedNames`, the names this emission would actually write, taken from the one cell array the body and the verifier already share (that array was spelled out twice and is now hoisted, so a third copy cannot drift from what `emittedNames` claims). And `checkP4ForPanel` now takes the `EmissionOk | null` rather than a `readonly string[]`, reaching for `emittedNames` itself.

The signature change is the fix. Adding the field alone would have left every call site one plausible-looking property access from the same defect, and no test of `checkP4ForPanel` could see the difference, because the wrong list is a perfectly good list. Moving the choice inside the function puts it next to the reasoning and leaves callers nothing to get wrong. Same rule this file already records for `ignore_terrain_restrictions` and `beachTerrain`: **the exception belongs inside the thing that computes the rule, not at the call site that knows about it.**

**`checkP4ForPanel` had no test coverage at all**, which is the whole reason this shipped. One manufactures a real collision and requires it still be reported. One pins that no emission is not a collision.

With `emittedNames` set to `[...verified.resolved.keys()]`, which is the original defect expressed in the one place it can now live, two tests go red naming 133 collisions starting at `RADIUS_PLAYER_LANDS`, reproducing the reported screen exactly. With the collision filter replaced by an empty array, the over-correction where P4 simply never fires again, one test goes red naming `DEGREES_SOLO`. Each mutant kills exactly the test that owns it. Both files restored from byte copies and diffed, per this file's own rule that the restore is where the damage happens.

**2026-09-02 (later still, third pass) — Per-player rings raised from a panel run, written up as Q10 rather than built.**

Asked for directly after the manual run: a ring's repeat count should be able to follow the player count, since a ring is usually a cycle over players, with the hand-wired path kept as the alternative. Two questions came out of it and they are at different maturity levels, which is the main thing the note records.

**The ring half is Sec.12 Q3's own deferred variant, and Q3 named the condition for reopening it.** Q3 resolved the count as user-chosen on 2026-08-29 and closed with "worth revisiting once patterns are built, because a pattern with one P slot and n repeats is already most of the way there". Patterns are built. So this is the spec's next step rather than a deviation from it, and the mechanism is already written down: a ladder of precomputed integer literals keyed on `n_PLAYER_GAME` labels, forced into that shape by two constraints pinned elsewhere (Sec.5.1, `if` cannot test a constant; Sec.5.4, every branch has to be integral or the trig macro breaks at 7).

**The finding that actually sizes the work is that the ladder solves the wrong half.** It makes the ANGLES runtime-correct and leaves the NUMBER of emitted `create_land` commands fixed, because a count is decided the moment text is written and no ladder over a step size changes how many commands are in the file. So a per-player ring still has to choose between emitting the maximum and relying on the extras being harmless, guarding each land with its own conditional, or staying an edit-time convenience that sets `repeats` from the current player count. **The choice rests on what `assign_to AT_PLAYER 7` does in a 4-player game, which Sec.4.5 asserts is ordinary and nobody has ever measured.** No RMSTEST varies player count against the assignment; the two files that mention `AT_PLAYER` hold it fixed. The outcomes differ enough to decide the design (land skipped, land placed unowned, or the command errors), and the observable is one script read back with `--clusters`. This is the standing rule about a fallback chosen against an undemonstrated failure mode, arriving on a feature that has not been built yet, which is the cheapest place to catch it.

**The chain half is not designed, and Sec.4.5 currently reads as though it were.** That section has a heading "Patterns and chains compose, and Bulls_Eyes needs both" and gives the requested example verbatim, a hexagonal ring of player lands each with two flanking neutrals. It is true one member at a time: every member `expandShapeGroup` builds is parented to `group.parent`, a child is parented to one member by id, and no form of `Placement.parent` means "every member of this group". Six members with two neutrals each is twelve placements wired by hand. The paragraph should be corrected whatever is decided, since it is the paragraph a reader goes to when asking this exact question.

**One thing already works and should not be rebuilt.** `reExpand.ts:248` refuses to delete a departing member that has a child and releases it instead, keeping its parent, label, children and last per-repeat literals, so hand-wired chains survive a repeat-count change rather than breaking. That is what makes the cheap option for the chain half viable.

**Recommendation, in the note.** Take the edit-time convenience first (a per-player checkbox mirroring `RandomParam.perPlayer` and `emittedForPlayerCount`, whose warning shape P2 already implements and tests), then measure, then reconsider the runtime ladder. Take the one-shot copy-onto-every-member action for the chain half, since it adds no invariant that can rot. **And note Sec.4.4's coupling, which is not optional**: a `perPlayer` RandomParam carries the same edit-time dependency and the document says the restriction "should be lifted here and there together or not at all", so the runtime version is one change across two features rather than a checkbox on rings.

**Written, not built**, per this repo's rule that an ambiguous or superseded spec gets escalated rather than improvised. `docs/land-placement-per-player-escalation.md` is new, with a Q10 pointer from Sec.12 so it is reachable from the authoritative document. No code changed in this pass and no test moved: the suite stands where the previous entry left it, 106 files / 2594 tests.

**2026-09-02 (fourth pass) — Per-player rings designed. The option the previous entry recommended was wrong, and the reason retires a measurement it called blocking.**

The previous entry offered "emit the maximum count and let the extras be harmless" as the cheap path, pending a measurement of `assign_to AT_PLAYER` overflow. **That option is dead however the measurement comes out**, and it took one sentence from the person who asked for the feature to see it: an 8 land ring has its lands 45 degrees apart, so removing one leaves the survivors 45 degrees apart and opens a single 90 degree gap. **Membership is not the only thing that changes with the count. The arrangement changes, and an arrangement is fixed the moment its angles are written.** The first draft had reasoned about which lands exist and never about where the remaining ones sit, which is the same shape as this file's own rule about a fix that removes the symptom without stating the rule.

**Two constraints found in the reference data decide the emission shape, and they were not in the design doc.** The `n_PLAYER_GAME` labels test an EXACT count, not a threshold: all eight are `verified: true` and each reads "Exactly N players in the game". And `controlKeywords` holds only `if`/`elseif`/`else`/`endif` with no boolean operator documented anywhere. **Flagged in the note as unproven rather than asserted**, per this repo's rule that reference data is a positive resolver and never a negative authority: a missing `or` in `language.json` is not evidence the engine lacks one, and the guide's Conditionals section should be read before anyone builds on it. It is an optimisation question either way, since the branch shape is correct with or without an `or`.

From the exact-count constraint alone there is no way to express "emit this land when the count is at least k", so the only expressible shape is **one complete arrangement per player count** inside a single `if`/`elseif` chain.

**This supersedes Sec.12 Q3's `ALP_STEP` ladder rather than using it**, which is the main design result. The ladder exists to make the step size runtime while the land count stays fixed; the count cannot stay fixed, so the ladder's reason to exist goes away. What replaces it is strictly simpler: every angle inside a branch is a plain integer literal computed at emit time, so Sec.5.4's integrality holds by construction at every count including 7 with no runtime division, and Sec.5.5's verification runs per branch against numbers the compiler already produces.

**Two things fall out for free.** The `assign_to AT_PLAYER 7` overflow measurement the previous entry called blocking is **retired**, because no branch ever emits a land for an absent player. And **the per-member chain question from two entries ago dissolves for per-player rings**: each branch is generated at a count the emitter knows, so "three aux per player" is ordinary expansion. It survives only for rings that are not per-player, dropping from a design question to a convenience.

**The cost is the sum over supported counts, not the maximum, and it is large.** A one-slot ring over counts 2-8 emits 35 lands and roughly 455 constants. A Bulls_Eyes shape, one player slot with three chained aux each, emits **140 lands and roughly 1,800 constants** against the 133 that map carries today. The note's first mitigation is a row of checkboxes letting the author pick supported counts, which takes 2/4/6/8 from 140 lands to 80 and is the main cost control. It also flags checking the emitted fence against `LIMITS.maxBlocksPerOutput`, since the consistency checker already had a real map rejected there and the user got nothing rather than a truncation.

**`create_player_lands` is named in the note as the case where none of this is needed.** The engine command creates one land per player natively with `circle_radius`, adapting to the count with no conditionals. It cannot replace the feature, since the tool never learns where the engine put each player and so has no `X_P1`/`Y_P1` to hang a chain off, but for a bare per-player ring with no children it is one command against 35 lands and the tool should offer it.

**Written as a design, not built**, at the owner's instruction that this session designs and an implementation session follows. `docs/land-placement-per-player-escalation.md` is rewritten from the earlier escalation into a design with a cost table, a five item implementation brief (distinct per-branch names so the flat cell list and every consumer of `resolved`/`quantities` survive untouched; preview at the current setting; what P2 becomes; the `else` branch, since an unsupported count otherwise emits silently nothing; chains needing nothing new) and four remaining decisions. Sec.12 Q10 is rewritten to match. No code changed and no test moved: 106 files / 2594 tests, as the second pass left it.

**2026-09-02 (fifth pass) — Per-player rings, revision 3. A threshold you cannot write can still be manufactured, and the emission drops from 140 lands to 32.**

Revision 2 (previous entry) established that the `n_PLAYER_GAME` labels test an exact count, concluded that "emit this land when the count is at least k" therefore cannot be expressed, and designed around that by emitting one complete arrangement per player count. The owner supplied the idiom that refutes it, taken from working scripts: a prologue that converts the exact count into cumulative `#define AT_LEAST_k` labels, after which `if AT_LEAST_5` is a working threshold anywhere in the file.

**The reasoning error is worth naming because it was not a missing fact.** Revision 2 had every constraint right, including Sec.5.1's own note that `if` tests a LABEL and never a constant, which is precisely what makes `#define` work here. It took "the labels provide no threshold" and concluded "the engine provides no threshold", treating a property of the vocabulary as a property of the language. **When a constraint blocks an expression, check whether the value can be computed once and stored before concluding the expression is unreachable.** The cost of not asking was a design emitting 140 lands where 32 do.

**Q3's `ALP_STEP` ladder is therefore used rather than superseded**, which reverses the previous entry's main result. The two halves are complementary and neither works alone: the ladder makes the ANGLES follow the count, the `AT_LEAST` labels make MEMBERSHIP follow it, and Q3 only ever had the first.

**Shape.** A prologue of eight branches carrying the cumulative labels and the per-count player angles; the existing frame algebra for every land, unconditional and unchanged; one two-line `if ALP_AT_LEAST_k` guard around each `create_land` owned by, or chained to, player k. Emission goes from revision 2's 35 lands and ~455 constants to **8 lands and ~104 plus a ~36 line prologue** for a one-slot ring, and from 140 to **32** for a Bulls_Eyes shape. The body is the size it is today.

**Angles are emitted per land per branch, not as one step constant per branch.** `theta = ROTATION + k * ALP_STEP` needs one constant instead of k but accumulates rounding error: at 7 players the step rounds 51.43 to 51 and by the seventh land nearly 3 degrees have collected in the final gap. Rounding each angle independently caps the error at 0.5 degrees with no accumulation, the same reasoning `expand.ts` already records for preferring rounding to truncation. The cost is a triangular sum, 36 constants across all eight branches.

**Three findings for the implementing session, in the note.** `#define` is a new emission kind with no value, so it cannot go through `verifyEmission`'s resolve-and-compare path and needs its own cell kind rather than a special case in the verifier. The prologue's names must go through `NameAllocator` and into `emittedNames` like everything else, and must NOT use the bare `AT_LEAST_3` spelling from the example, since a script carrying its own prologue would shadow the tool's or be shadowed by it. And the conditional structure must be emitted from a structure that cannot unbalance, with a balance assertion over the rendered fence: the owner's own source example carries a comment marking an `endif` whose necessity was unclear and a warning that the nesting may not balance, which is the strongest available argument for the tool owning this block rather than the author.

**Two of revision 2's four open questions were artefacts of revision 2 and are retired, not answered.** "Which counts ship as supported" existed only because each count cost a full arrangement; the prologue covers 1 through 8 for a fixed cost, so all eight branches are always emitted and there is no checkbox row. "What does the `else` branch do" is unreachable for the same reason, and no `else` should be emitted, since it could only be dead code implying a case the enumeration already covers. The owner also rejected offering `create_player_lands` for the bare case: this tool is for advanced generation and anyone wanting the simple path already knows that command.

**Design only, no code**, at the owner's instruction that an implementation session follows. `docs/land-placement-per-player-escalation.md` rewritten to revision 3, keeping both prior corrections since each names a way of reasoning that failed; Sec.12 Q10 rewritten to match. Suite untouched at 106 files / 2594 tests.

**2026-09-02 (sixth pass) — Per-player rings, revision 4: authored angles. Three of the four rules already work, and Bulls_Eyes is the worked example. Sec.4.5's composition paragraph corrected.**

The owner asked whether a scripter can still customise angles under the prologue design, giving three cases: P2 at a minimum separation from P1, P2 at a fixed offset, and P2 at a fixed offset with variance. **The answer is that the model already does all three, and the map this whole tool was designed around is the proof.** `Bulls_Eyes.rms:20` and `:131` read `#const DIST_BW_PLAYERS rnd(80,280)` then `#const DEGREES_P2 (DIST_BW_PLAYERS + ROTATION_PLAYER)`, which is exactly "P2 spawns at a random bearing at least 80 degrees from P1". The hoisted `rnd` and the reference to it are forced by Sec.5.1's rule that `rnd` cannot sit inside an expression, and they are the shape `paramEmit.ts` already emits for every `RandomParam`.

**So the finding is a documentation failure in this note rather than a gap in the model.** `Placement.offset.theta` and `PatternSlot.theta` have been `Expr` since slice 1, the formula field has been the authoring surface since slice 5, and `RandomParam` already hoists. Revisions 1 through 3 each wrote "the angles" as though they were a property of the ring, and none of them checked what the type actually allows. **The only genuinely new requirement is that a rule may differ per player count**, and the prologue already branches per count, so that is where a per-count rule goes.

**That vindicates 4.1's per-land angle choice for a second reason.** Revision 3 chose to emit one angle constant per land per branch, rather than a shared `ALP_STEP`, on rounding-accuracy grounds: a shared step drifts nearly 3 degrees into the final gap at 7 players. A shared step also cannot express a per-land rule at all, so the accuracy argument and the authoring requirement point the same way.

**The body never changes when an angle is customised**, which is the property that keeps this from exploding. It references `ALP_DEG_Pk` and does not care how that value was reached, so customising one player's angle at one count edits one line inside one branch. An authored rule adds at most one hoisted `rnd` constant per rule, not per count.

**One guarantee stated and one refused.** RMS cannot solve constraints at runtime, so "no two players within 30 degrees" is not something the emission can promise. What it can do is draw within bounds that make the constraint true by construction: for two players that is Bulls_Eyes' own `rnd(80,280)`, and for n players it is even spacing plus bounded jitter, where the tool knows n inside each branch and can compute the largest safe jitter for that count and warn or clamp beyond it. **That is a real thing the tool can do that a hand-writer cannot**, and it is the shape the minimum-separation affordance should take. Free bearings can still collide, and the note says the panel must say so rather than imply a guarantee, in the same spirit as the drag refusal messages.

**Sec.4.4's restriction is lifted, as its own rule requires.** `perPlayer` parameters should emit at the maximum of 8 under a per-player ring, with unused draws harmless, so the edit-time count dependency goes away for them at the same time as for rings. Sec.4.4 says the lift must cover both "together or not at all", so this satisfies the rule rather than sidestepping it.

**Sec.4.5's "Patterns and chains compose" paragraph is corrected**, closing the item that had been carried as open since the third pass. It now separates the two cases the old sentence conflated: a per-player ring DOES repeat the chain, because each child is guarded by its parent's own `AT_LEAST_k` label, while a fixed-count ring does not, because `Placement.parent` names one anchor and nothing means "every member of this group". It also records why the manual path does not rot, which is `reExpand`'s departure rule releasing a member that has children rather than deleting it.

**Design only, no code.** Note at revision 4 with a new section 5 (the four rules, per-count mechanism, what can and cannot be guaranteed, the Sec.4.4 lift) and a seventh implementation item pinning that an angle rule inherits the existing drag refusal, since a per-count rule makes that path more likely to be hit rather than less. Suite untouched at 106 files / 2594 tests.

**2026-09-02 (seventh pass) — Per-player rings, revision 5: the model types pinned, a slice plan, and one silent-nothing failure found in the design's own "unreachable" claim.**

Asked whether the design was ready to hand to an implementation session. It was not, and saying so found a real defect.

**The three holes.** Revisions 1 to 4 settled what the emission looks like and left the types to the reader, which this repo's own rule says to escalate rather than let a session improvise. (1) Nothing said how a ring becomes per-player or what happens to `repeats` and `members` when the count is runtime. (2) Nothing said how the even angle reaches a member's theta, given `expandShapeGroup` currently bakes a literal and is pure with no allocator. (3) Nothing said where a per-count override lives in the model.

**The pinned answers.** A `ShapeGroup.perPlayer` boolean, with `repeats` held at `MAX_PLAYER_COUNT` while it is set, so `expandShapeGroup`, `memberKeyAt` and the merge rule keep operating on a fixed member list and need no change; Sec.4.5 already makes a repeat index a player index, so `assignToPlayer` and `ZonePolicy.perRepeat` come along untouched, and `shapeGroupLandTotal` is the only place that has to learn "up to". **The emitter owns per-player angles, not the expander**: expansion keeps baking the even literal at the maximum count so the model stays well formed and drawable, and `emitAlpModel` substitutes a reference to the prologue constant it allocates. Explicitly **do not** add an `Expr` leaf kind for this, which was the tempting shape: `Expr` is published contract in `tools-api/index.ts` with generated types behind it, and the emitter can do it locally where the allocator already lives. Per-count overrides go on the `Placement` as `thetaPerCount`, not on the `PatternSlot`, because "P2 is 30 degrees from P1" is about one member while a slot repeats across all of them, and members are already individually editable Placements carrying `nudged`.

**The defect, found while checking the constants rather than reasoning.** `MIN_PLAYER_COUNT` is 2, so revision 3 wrote the prologue as covering 2 through 8 and declared the no-branch-matches case unreachable. **A 1 player game then matches nothing, defines no `AT_LEAST` label and emits no lands at all**, which is exactly the silent-nothing failure that claim was about. The app's own settings bound is about what can be AUTHORED and says nothing about what a published map meets in the wild, and `1_PLAYER_GAME` is a real label. The prologue covers 1 through 8. **An enumeration is only exhaustive over the domain it actually enumerates, and the authoring tool's range is not the runtime's range** — same shape as this file's existing rule that a corpus total is not a corpus measurement.

**Slice plan, since one handoff would be too large and this repo does not work that way.** Slice A is the core and delivers the ask on its own: `perPlayer`, the prologue, the guards, the checkbox, preview at the current count, P2 standing down. Slice B is mostly verification rather than construction, since three of the four angle rules already work, plus the `perPlayer` RandomParam lift. Slice C is per-count rules and the bounded-jitter helper. **Sec.10.1's acceptance gate does not move**: Bulls_Eyes is a fixed-count map with `perPlayer` false everywhere, it must stay byte-identical through all three slices, and it is the regression test that this feature did not disturb the existing path.

Design only, no code. Suite untouched at 106 files / 2594 tests.

**2026-09-03 — Land Placement Slice A built (`docs/land-placement-per-player-slice-a-brief.md`): `ShapeGroup.perPlayer`, the eight-branch prologue, one guard per player-owned land, the panel checkbox, and preview at the current count. All six of the brief's own hazards avoided; a seventh, unnamed problem found and fixed along the way.**

Read the escalation note's Sections 2, 3, 4, 7 and 8 and the design doc's Sec.4.5, Sec.5.1, Sec.5.4, Sec.5.6, Sec.6.1 and Sec.12 Q3/Q10 before writing anything, per the brief's own §0 list, then `emitModel.ts`, `compiler/verify.ts` and `compiler/emit.ts` together, since items 2 and 3 change all three as one pipeline. `expand.ts` was read and not touched.

**The model.** `ShapeGroup` gained `perPlayer: boolean` (`model.ts`), pinning `repeats` at `MAX_PLAYER_COUNT` while set. `expandShapeGroup`, `memberKeyAt` and `reExpand`'s merge rule are all untouched, exactly as item 1 intends: a repeat index already reads as a player index (Sec.4.5), so the only ripple was adding the field to every test fixture that builds a `ShapeGroup` literal by hand (`expand.test.ts`, `emitModel.test.ts`'s defensive-fill case, `reExpand.test.ts`, `panel/__tests__/modelOps.test.ts`) and to `modelOps.ts`'s `addRing`.

**A new module, `prologue.ts`, owns the whole per-player mechanism**, kept out of `emitModel.ts` itself since it is a self-contained piece with its own naming, its own conditional-text builder and its own guard-propagation walk. `buildPrologue` takes a model's `perPlayer` groups plus the raw, pre-param-resolution placement list and returns the rendered eight-branch `if`/`elseif`/`endif` text, every name it allocated, a theta override per group member (item 4), a guard label per placement propagated down `parent` chains so a chained aux land inherits its ring member's own `ALP_AT_LEAST_k` (item 6, and the escalation's own "patterns and chains compose" correction), and two separate DEG cell sets, below. `renderConditionalBlock` builds the conditional text from a branch list rather than string concatenation — item 6's own stated hazard — so there is no code path that omits its own `endif` or emits a stray `elseif`; it is shared between the prologue's own eight-branch ladder and each individual `create_land` guard, so both hazards are the same guarantee rather than two.

**The two DEG cell sets are the one real design wrinkle neither the brief nor the escalation note named.** `emitAlpModel` already had to resolve `ALP_DEG_Pk` only for the previewed count (Sec.7.4), leaving players beyond it deliberately unresolved so the overlay only ever draws that many lands. Feeding that same restricted set into `verifyEmission`'s cross-check produced a false positive on every unpreviewed player: `evalExpr`'s strict AST propagation and `evaluateExpressionTokens`'s RMS-faithful "drop an unresolved operand after the first" (Sec.5.1) only ever agree once every operand genuinely resolves, and the SIN/COS macro's own `P` cell (`180 * S - R * R`) starts with a literal `180`, so an unresolved player's `S`/`R` still lets the token walk silently resolve `P` to `180` while the AST evaluator correctly reports the whole expression unresolvable. **Neither evaluator is wrong; nothing before this feature ever asked them to agree on a genuinely partial resolve.** The fix keeps two DEG cell sets rather than touching either evaluator: `liveDegCells` (the previewed count only, feeds the `resolved` map the panel and overlay read) and `crossCheckDegCells` (every player, at the group's own pinned maximum count, matching what `expandShapeGroup` already bakes for a fixed-count ring). `emitModel.ts` now calls `verifyEmission` twice — once against the fully-resolved set to catch a real compiler bug, once with no targets at all, purely to build the previewed `resolved` map.

**`emitModel.ts`'s new Step 1.5** resolves a `perPlayer` group's `rotation` through the same param resolver every other `Expr` in this function goes through, builds the prologue, then substitutes each member's baked-literal theta for a `sym` reference to its own prologue constant before the frame algebra runs (Sec.8.2 — `frame.ts` needed no change at all, since a `sym` leaf lowers exactly like any other). The body stays unconditional at the pinned maximum count (item 4.2); only the `create_land` skeletons get wrapped, one guard each.

**`shapeGroupLandTotal`** (`viewModel.ts`) now returns `{ count, exact }` rather than a bare number, since a `perPlayer` ring's land count is an upper bound, not the count the map actually emits at any given player count. The ring editor prints "up to N lands" for one and "N lands" for the other, and gained a per-player checkbox — `HelpTip`-wrapped with a matching `ui-help.json` entry, per this file's own hard rule — that pins `repeats` to `MAX_PLAYER_COUNT` when checked and disables the Repeats field with a title explaining why.

**P2 needed no code change**, which is worth stating rather than leaving as a silent absence: it only ever fires on a `RandomParam.perPlayer` mismatch (`preconditions.ts`'s `checkP2`), and this slice's angle mechanism never creates or references one, so it stands down by construction, matching item 8's own text.

**Acceptance, all from the brief's own §2.** A one-slot `perPlayer` ring emits 8 lands, a prologue of 8 branches, and exactly 7 guarded `create_land` skeletons — player 1 needs none. `emittedNames` carries every `ALP_AT_LEAST_*` and `ALP_DEG_*` name across all eight branches, not only the previewed one. P4 reports no collision on a clean script and still reports one when a name is genuinely taken. The rendered fence is balanced at every count, asserted directly by counting `if`/`endif` occurrences rather than eyeballing the text.

**Mutation-tested, restored by re-editing rather than a byte copy** (the file is small enough to read back in full each time and confirm the diff by eye): dropping `renderConditionalBlock`'s own `lines.push("endif")` turned five balance-dependent tests red; letting player 1 pick up a guard (`atLeastNames.get(playerIndex + 1) ?? "ALP_AT_LEAST_1"`, chosen so the map lookup itself could not mask the mutant the way a bare boundary flip did on the first attempt) turned the "player 1 needs no guard" tests red in both `prologue.test.ts` and `emitModel.test.ts`; disabling chain-parent propagation turned the composition tests red. All three restored and reconfirmed green.

**Sec.10.1's Bulls_Eyes acceptance gate is untouched and green, and was never at risk**: `acceptance.test.ts` calls `buildFrame`/`emitCells` directly over hand-built `Placement`s, never `emitAlpModel` or anything in `prologue.ts`, so this slice could not have reached it either way.

**Verification.** `npm run typecheck`, `npm run lint` (0 errors, the same pre-existing warnings every prior slice has carried), `npm run validate:reference` (the new `landPlacement.perPlayer` `ui-help.json` entry validates and round-trips). Full `npm test`: **109 files / 2609 tests, 161.75s, floor 68/1651** — new: `prologue.ts`'s own `prologue.test.ts` (13 tests); extended: `emitModel.test.ts` (+6, the per-player acceptance block) and `panel/__tests__/viewModel.test.ts` (+1, the upper-bound case); fixture-only: `expand.test.ts`, `reExpand.test.ts`, `panel/__tests__/modelOps.test.ts` (each gained `perPlayer: false` on an existing literal, no behaviour change). The arithmetic from the entering baseline (106/2594) does not account for all of this row on its own — this file's own standing caveat about parallel-session drift applies as usual.

**Owed: a manual `npm run tauri dev` pass**, since nothing in this environment can render `LandPlacementPanel.tsx` (the standing constraint every prior UI slice has hit). Run sheet:

1. Open a script, select the Land Placement tool, add a role and a ring (`+ Role`, `+ Ring`).
2. Check "One land per player" on the ring. Confirm the Repeats field disables and shows a title explaining why, and the ring's own label switches to "up to 8 lands".

Confirm the preconditions strip shows no P4 collisions, and switch to the Code tab to read the emitted fence: one prologue with eight `if`/`elseif`/`endif` branches at the top, `ALP_AT_LEAST_*` defines and `ALP_DEG_P*` consts inside each, then the unconditional frame algebra, then eight `create_land` blocks lower in the section, seven of them wrapped in their own guard.
6. Change the player count again post-Apply and regenerate (or re-open the Preview tab) to confirm the SCRIPT itself, not just the panel, produces the right count of lands at runtime — this is the one step nothing short of a real generation can check.
7. Try adding a chained aux land off one of the ring's members (parent it to a specific `ring#i#P` placement) and confirm, after Apply, that its own `create_land` is wrapped in the SAME guard as its parent rather than left unguarded or given its own.

**2026-09-03 (later) — Land Placement Slice B built (`docs/land-placement-per-player-slice-b-brief.md`): authored angles survive into the prologue, the `perPlayer` `RandomParam` restriction lifted, the drag refusal extended to a per-player member, and one real ordering bug (hazard 2) found while proving item 2 rather than argued about in advance.**

The brief's own framing held: three of the four angle rules already worked (`Placement.offset.theta`/`PatternSlot.theta` have been `Expr` since slice 1, the formula field since slice 5, `RandomParam` hoisting since this same day's earlier slice-5 work), so this session wrote nine new tests across three existing files and touched no new file at all — the whole point being verification, not construction, per the brief's own instruction not to manufacture work.

**Item 1: a ring member's own theta was NOT reachable, and now is.** `PlacementEditor` gated its ENTIRE polar offset block (`Radius` and `Angle (deg)` both) behind `!inGroup`, correctly hiding Parent/Frame (which a member takes from its group) but incorrectly hiding the one field Sec.5.1's whole authoring surface depends on. Fixed narrowly — only the `Angle` field is now shown for a group member, `Radius` stays hidden — and its `onCommit` now goes through `applyDragToPlacement` (already used by canvas drags) instead of the bare `updatePlacement`, so editing a member's angle from the panel stamps `nudged: true` exactly the way a canvas drag does, which is what item 2's "has a rule" detection reads. No automated test pins the JSX gating itself (this repo's own established practice for `LandPlacementPanel.tsx`, per every prior slice's "manual tauri run sheet" entry — nothing in this environment can render it); the underlying model-level behaviour it now makes reachable is what items 2 and 4's own tests pin end to end.

**Item 2, the whole slice: `prologue.ts` gained a one-time pass, before the per-count branch loop, that decides whether each group member "has a rule."** A member has one when `nudged === true`, or when its current `offset.theta` is not `exprEquals` to the exact `bin` `expand.ts` itself would have baked for that member at the group's own (maximum, for a `perPlayer` group) `repeats` — deliberately never `evalClosed`, since the even default's own baked expression (`add(rotation, num(angle))`) is JUST as literal-shaped as an authored rewrite to a different literal; only structural comparison against the specific default tells them apart. A member with a rule uses that member's own theta (param-resolved with `ownerPlayer = playerIndex + 1`, threading `emitModel.ts`'s existing `resolveExprParams` closure straight through as a new `buildPrologue` parameter) in EVERY branch it appears in, unchanged by count; a member with none keeps recomputing the even default per branch exactly as slice A left it. Confirmed by mutation: reverting the rule lookup to always use the even default turned three tests red (two new, one already-passing regression check that a default-matching placement still varies by count) and left everything else green.

**Hazard 2, found rather than argued: the prologue was landing BEFORE the param cells it can now reference, not after.** `emitModel.ts`'s own body assembly had `prologue.text` first, followed by `paramEmission.cells`/`roleCells`/`frameCells` — correct through slice A, where nothing in a prologue DEG cell ever referenced a param name, and silently wrong the instant item 2 let one (Bulls_Eyes' own `DEGREES_P2 = DIST_BW_PLAYERS + ROTATION_PLAYER` shape, rebuilt as a per-player rule) reach the body. `verifyEmission`'s own cross-check pass had ALWAYS fed itself `paramEmission.cells` before `prologue.crossCheckDegCells` — its internal resolve order was already correct — so this was purely a rendered-TEXT ordering bug the verifier's own array-order logic could never have caught, and the first attempt at the new item-2 test caught it immediately (`indexOf` asserting the param cell precedes the DEG line). Fixed by splitting the body into three ordered pieces — param lines, then the prologue (if any), then role/frame lines — rather than the previous two; byte-identical to before for any script with no `perPlayer` group, since that reduces to the same three pieces in the same order they always were.

**Item 3: `emitRandomParams` no longer takes a `playerCount` at all** — every `perPlayer` `RandomParam` emits one cell per player up to `MAX_PLAYER_COUNT` (8) unconditionally, ring or not, per Sec.4.4's own "lifted here and there together or not at all." `applyEdits.ts`'s `withEmittedPlayerCounts` (which used to stamp `RandomParam.emittedForPlayerCount` with the live count on every Apply) is deleted outright — there is no longer a count to stamp. **P2 was checked for a live caller before anything was touched, per the brief's own hazard 3, and it has one**: `LandPlacementPanel.tsx` still calls `checkP2` and renders `p2Mismatches`. `checkP2` itself is untouched; it simply has nothing left to fire on for anything this tool emits, since nothing sets `emittedForPlayerCount` to a value that could ever mismatch the live count any more. `docs/land-placement-design.md` Sec.4.4 updated in place (strikethrough plus a replacement paragraph, matching this doc's own convention for a superseded standing limitation) rather than silently rewritten.

**Item 4: `applyDrag` gained an `isPerPlayerMember` boolean** (default `false`, so every existing call site and test is unaffected). When set, it forces `"Angle"` into the symbolic-decline set for a `polar` offset unconditionally, on top of whatever `evalClosed` already found — because a per-player member's theta is unconditionally replaced by `sym(ALP_DEG_Pk)` at emission time regardless of the member's own literal shape (item 2's own default case bakes a fully-literal `bin`, evaluable by `evalClosed`, that the emitter still discards). `dragMath.ts` has no notion of `ShapeGroup`; the caller (`LandPlacementCanvas.tsx`'s `handlePlacementDrag`) computes the flag from `groupForMember(model, placementId)?.perPlayer === true` and passes it through, the same shape `emitModel.ts` itself uses to decide the substitution. **Mutation-tested with the fixture the brief's own hazard 4 asks for**: the new decline test reuses the EXACT `bin("+", num(30), num(15))` fixture an existing test already proves DOES resolve and DOES drag without the flag — deleting the `isPerPlayerMember` forcing line turned that test and one other red while leaving the rest of the suite green, confirming the fixture genuinely distinguishes the guarded and unguarded code rather than merely reproducing an already-symbolic case.

**Verification.** `npm run typecheck`, `npm run lint` (0 errors, the same pre-existing warnings every prior slice has carried), `npm run validate:reference` (unaffected, no reference-data change this slice). Full `npm test`: **109 files / 2618 tests, 121.01 s** — the arithmetic from slice A's own 109/2609 is +9 exactly (3 in `prologue.test.ts`, 4 in `panel/__tests__/dragMath.test.ts`, 2 in `emitModel.test.ts`), no parallel-session drift this time. Sec.10.1's Bulls_Eyes acceptance gate (`acceptance.test.ts`) re-run and still green — it calls `buildFrame`/`emitCells` directly and never touches `prologue.ts` or `paramEmit.ts`'s new signature, so it could not have been at risk either way, same as slice A's own note.

**Owed, same standing constraint every UI-touching slice has carried: a manual `npm run tauri dev` pass.** Extends slice A's own run sheet rather than replacing it: build a per-player ring, select a non-P1 member, confirm the Angle field is now visible and editable, type a formula referencing another member or a `RandomParam` (e.g. `ALP_DIST_BW_PLAYERS + ALP_ROTATION`), confirm the canvas redraws that member off the new rule at the current player count, confirm dragging that member declines with a stated reason and leaves the model unchanged, Apply, and read the fence: the referenced param's own `#const rnd(...)` cell should appear before the prologue, and the authored member's own `ALP_DEG_Pk` line should read the formula (not a number) in every branch from its own player count through 8.

**Still open.** Slice C (`Placement.thetaPerCount`, the panel surface for a per-count rule, and the bounded-jitter helper) is unstarted, as scoped — nothing in this slice built any part of it, and a `perPlayer` member's rule (once it has one) is still the SAME expression in every branch, exactly as Sec.5.2 describes for the case slice B covers.

Six real-engine exports came back today (RMSTEST_65-69 from Batch 14/15, written 2026-08-30 and 2026-09-02's own `RMSTEST_70`, written this session to chase down why `AD4 - Pag - v1.2.rms`'s preview showed land bordering water with no beach).
