## 2026-09-29 preview-design rev 8, land growth from genie-rms (spec only)

Spec and docs only, and no generator code changed. The request was for the land stage to work the way the engine's does, with approval to port genie-rms and to credit it.

**What changed.**

- `docs/preview-design.md` is at rev 8. Sec.6.1's growth is replaced by a port of genie-rms's `LandGenerator.js` and `cleanTerrain`, written as eleven numbered rules. Sec.11 item 1, Sec.13 (five new gates), Sec.15 (items 43 to 48 opened, item 18 withdrawn, item 32 retired) and Appendix A follow from it. The rev 7 changelog moved here, beside the rev 6 one.
- BUG-036 filed in `docs/known-issues.md`.
- Credits. `CreditsSettings.tsx` thanks genie-rms, and an adjacent sibling CSS rule gives two consecutive thank-you paragraphs a gap without moving the first one. `README.md` gained a Credits section naming Zetnus and genie-rms. PLAN.md's open question 1 already required crediting Zetnus in the README, and the README never did.

**How the port was checked.** A throwaway JavaScript simulation of the port's rules, kept in a scratch folder and not tracked, ran against RMSTEST_21, 23, 38 and 73 at their exact fixture parameters. The figures are in Sec.6.1's table. Sec.13's gates re-derive them against the real implementation once it is built, and those are the figures to trust.

**The one check against DE itself.** The port's cleanup pass predicts that no land tile is left with base terrain on both opposite sides. `AoE2ScenarioParser` over the 21 exports of RMSTEST_21, 23, 28, 28b and 38 in `tools/scenario-probe/generated-tests/` found zero such tiles on every export. The simulated RMSTEST_38 map has 74 to 102 per run without the pass. Set `PYTHONIOENCODING=utf-8` before loading scenarios from a script on this machine, or the parser's progress glyphs crash on cp1252.

**BUG-036, found by running the shipped generator on RMSTEST_73.** The growers came out flush against the ICE walls, gap 1 on seeds 1 to 3, against DE's 7, 11 and 13. The probe was a throwaway test file run by exact path and deleted straight after.

**Sec.6.1 growth text removed by rev 8, word for word.**

> **Connectedness is a function of `clumping_factor`, and the frontier model survives with one bucket changed. MEASURED (RMSTEST_38, 2026-08-04, five distinct maps, six `cf` values on one map).** A single `create_land` does _not_ always come back in one piece — but whether it does is governed entirely by `clumping_factor`:
>
> | `clumping_factor`            | −20       | 0     | 8 (default) | 20    | 40    | 100   |
> | ---------------------------- | --------- | ----- | ----------- | ----- | ----- | ----- |
> | 4-connected pieces           | 6–10      | 1–5   | 1–2         | **1** | **1** | **1** |
> | circularity of largest piece | 0.133     | 0.181 | 0.360       | 0.409 | 0.428 | 0.463 |
> | tiles against a declared 400 | **−6.5%** | +4.6% | +3.3%       | +3.2% | +3.6% | +4.1% |
>
> **Piece count falls monotonically and reaches a hard 1 by `cf 20`**, which is inside the corpus's own common band (15–25) — so ordinary maps never see this and the effect is confined to the low end. Identical under 8-connectivity, so the pieces are genuinely disconnected rather than a diagonal snake split by the probe's 4-connectivity.
>
> **Normative model:** `clumping_factor` sets how strongly growth prefers candidates adjacent to the land's existing mass. Above ~20 growth is pure frontier expansion exactly as described below. Below ~20 a land's turn may instead place a tile **detached from its existing mass**, seeding a new component, with the probability rising as `cf` falls. **So the weight-bucket machinery, the guide:927 regimes and the round-robin turn structure all stand; what changes is that a turn has a second, rarer source of candidates.** This is the cheap repair, and the expensive alternative (growth is not frontier-based at any setting) is refuted by `cf ≥ 20` giving exactly one piece in fifteen consecutive land generations.
>
> **Where the detached tile comes from — this is the part that has to be specified, and it is not the weight.** Rev 6 wrote the repair as "bucket index 0 exists", weighted by `neighborsOwned = 0`. That does not implement: the frontier is _defined_ as candidates 4-adjacent to owned tiles, so every candidate in it has `neighborsOwned ≥ 1` and a bucket 0 keyed off that count is unreachable by construction. An implementer following the growth paragraph below would have produced the pre-repair model and never seen the `cf −20` fragmentation at all. The weight is also the fittable half; the **candidate source** is the modelling choice, and leaving that open is leaving the wrong thing open.
>
> **Normative form.** At land start, sample a small **detached-seed reservoir** of `R` **[tune]** tiles — rejection-sampled by the same origin rules the land's own origin used (inside borders, inside the cross unless `generate_mode 1`, not owned) — and hold it alongside the frontier. Each turn, with probability `w(cf)` **[tune]**, the land draws from the reservoir instead of the frontier; the drawn tile is claimed and its empty 4-neighbours enter the normal weight buckets, so the new component grows by the ordinary rule from then on. `w(cf)` is 0 at `cf ≥ 20` and rises as `cf` falls, fitted against the piece counts in the table above (6–10 at `cf −20`, 1–5 at 0, 1–2 at 8). Reservoir draws are O(1) and the reservoir is a fixed-size `Int32Array`, so **Sec.11's frontier structure and its 40 ms budget are untouched** — which a bucket whose candidate set is "every unowned tile" would not be, since that is a scan.
>
> Two properties this form is chosen to preserve, both from the RMSTEST_38 measurement: piece sizes at `cf −20` were **comparable rather than one-large-plus-crumbs** (a reservoir sampled once at land start, with every seed then growing in the same round-robin, reproduces that; seeding lazily on demand does not), and fragmentation is a function of `cf` alone with no dependence on land size or map size. **Both `R` and `w(cf)` are `[tune]` and the _form_ is a modelling choice, not a measurement** — what is measured is the piece-count column, and any mechanism reproducing it is admissible. Tracked as Sec.15 item 18.
>
> **A second finding, and it is separate from connectedness: at `cf −20` growth does not meet its budget.** Every other setting overshoots by the familiar +3 to +4.6% (Sec.4's growth overshoot); `cf −20` comes in **6.5% short**, 374 tiles against 400, and one run reached only 340. A land scattering into ten fragments evidently exhausts its placement attempts before spending its budget. Model it as a real shortfall and report `growthShortfall` (Sec.7) rather than silently truncating.
>
> **`clumping_factor 100` is accepted and is not clamped**, which matters because **17 uses across the 32 tracked maps write exactly that** (18 counting `test-maps/local/`) and community sources give the maximum as 99. It produced one piece in every run with the highest circularity in the sweep — though the 20 → 100 circularity rise (0.409 → 0.463) sits inside the run-to-run spread, so treat "more circular than `cf 20`" as unproven and "accepted, behaves like a high value" as measured. Consistent with RMSTEST_20/21's finding that circularity saturates near 15–20.
>
> **Growth — synchronized frontier expansion:** all lands grow in round-robin turns, one tile per unfinished land per round (this approximates "growth happens all at once"). Per turn, a land draws from the detached-seed reservoir with probability `w(cf)` (above), and otherwise samples from its frontier (empty candidates 4-adjacent to owned tiles) by weight. The frontier is held in **integer weight buckets** (Sec.11) — bucket index is a function of `neighborsOwned ∈ [1,4]` and the land's clumping regime, sampling is O(1), and no `Math.pow` is involved (goal 5). The `[1,4]` range is exhaustive _for the frontier_, which is why fragmentation needs the reservoir and not a fifth bucket. Regimes follow guide:927, minus its 40+ row:
>
> | `clumping_factor` | Guide:927                                     | Model                                                                                                        |
> | ----------------- | --------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
> | negative          | "extremely snakey, generally not recommended" | strongly favour `neighborsOwned == 1`                                                                        |
> | 0 and above       | "more irregular lands" → "rounder lands"      | weight rises **continuously** with `neighborsOwned`, steepness ramping with `cf` and saturating by `cf ≈ 15` |
>
> **MEASURED (RMSTEST_21, 2026-08-01), and this replaces a four-row table with two rows.** Two things were wrong:
>
> **The 40+ directional regime does not exist.** Six lands of 600 tiles at `cf` −5/0/8/25/40/60, one per regime:
>
> | `cf` | circularity | bbox aspect |
> | ---- | ----------- | ----------- |
> | 8    | 0.265       | 1.50        |
> | 25   | 0.391       | 1.38        |
> | 40   | 0.384       | 1.24        |
> | 60   | **0.394**   | **1.05**    |
>
> `cf 60` came back the **roundest and least elongated** land of the six, and 40 and 60 are indistinguishable from 25. Rev 3 through rev 6 modelled it as a per-land preferred direction with weight rising on the projection onto it — an invention built on one guide sentence, and it would have drawn peninsulas the engine never draws. Deleted.
>
> **The regime boundaries are not steps.** Circularity ramps smoothly with no discontinuity at the guide's stated boundaries (see Sec.6.4's terrain table, measured the same day, where the ramp is clearest). Rev 4's warning against collapsing to a monotonic weight was aimed at preserving the 40+ peninsula; with that regime gone the warning inverts, and **a continuous weight is now the closer model**. Only the negative case stays special, and it is dramatic rather than marginal.
>
> Default 8 for lands (guide:925). A candidate is rejected if:
>
> - **outside a border.** `border_fuzziness` is an _adherence_ percentage `f` (default 20; guide:903). **MEASURED (RMSTEST_23, 2026-08-01): `f = 0` switches the border off entirely, and any `f > 0` is very nearly a hard stop.** Six runs on a 200 map with the border at tile 80 and a land pressing hard against it from tile 90:
>
>   | `f` | min x per run          | mean penetration |
>   | --- | ---------------------- | ---------------- |
>   | 0   | 63, 57, 66, 66, 81, 60 | **14.5 tiles**   |
>   | 20  | 78, 78, 78, 78, 81, 81 | **1.0**          |
>   | 50  | 79, 79, 80, 79, 79, 79 | **0.8**          |
>   | 100 | 80, 80, 80, 80, 80, 81 | **−0.2**         |
>
>   **Normative form: reject any candidate beyond the border when `f > 0`, except for a single fringe tile accepted with probability ≈ `(100−f)/100`.** That reproduces 1.0 at the default and 0.8 at 50 without an unbounded tail. `f = 0` → always accepted (borders ignored); `f = 100` or negative → `d ≥ 1` never accepted. **`f = 100` stopped on exactly tile 80 in five of six runs, so Sec.4's border tile arithmetic is right to the tile** — the cleanest single reading in the batch, since it is a hard boundary rather than a distribution.
>
>   Both prior models are dead, and they erred in the same direction. Rev 3's single depth-independent Bernoulli accepts 80% of the first ring _and_ 80% of the ring beyond, dissolving the border. Rev 4 corrected it to `d` independent Bernoulli(`f`/100) rolls, geometric decay with a mean of a few tiles — closer, and still far too permissive: over an edge this long that model reaches depth 4+ nearly every run, against a measured 1. The lesson is not the constant. **Two rounds of reasoning about the shape of a distribution moved the answer in the right direction and stopped well short of it, and one map settled it.** The closed form `((100−f)/100)^d` is retained here only as the historical model, and Sec.8's ban on `Math.pow`/`**` no longer bears on the implementation at all, since the rule is now a single roll;
>
> - within `other_zone_avoidance_distance` (the **smaller** of the two lands' values — guide) of a tile owned by a different zone (zone −12 exempt). **MEASURED AND CONFIRMED, 2026-09-03 (BUG-016, Sec.15).** A 2026-09-02 pass struck this bullet on a bounding-box read of RMSTEST_66's positive control (`gap = min_x(right) − max_x(left)` over each land's full bbox), which came back -3/-10/-5 and was taken as overlap. That was a measurement error: growth is a randomised frontier process, so two lands' bounding boxes can cross on paper — one bulging right at one y, the other bulging left at a different y — without the patches ever actually touching. Re-measured with the TRUE tile-to-tile minimum distance instead of bbox extent: the same control pair sat 5-7 tiles apart across all four runs, zero tiles of contact in every one. `RMSTEST_73` (one grower against a static, non-competing different-zone land, placed far enough away that its origin doesn't already start inside its own declared distance) calibrated the model exactly — measured gap = declared value + 1, for three different declared values, reproducing across three runs. RMSTEST_66's own asymmetric pair (radius 12 vs 2), re-read the same way, confirms "the smaller wins": a 3-7 tile gap across four runs, three of the four landing on exactly 2+1=3, nowhere near the 12+1=13 "larger wins" would predict. `RMSTEST_74` separately confirmed the origin-time half with a properly-powered design (RMSTEST_71's clean pass had ~60-80% chance of happening with zero enforcement; RMSTEST_74's 20-competing-origins design cut that to ~1% and still passed clean). `lands.ts`'s `violatesZoneAvoidance` is restored.
> - already owned.
>
> A land stops at target, or when its frontier is exhausted — recording a `growthShortfall` report (owned/target, dominant blocker among border/zone/space) for 5.2's land layer. `land_conformity` is **not simulated** (buggy in-engine, guide advises avoiding it) — SimulationNote when present.

**Sec.11 item 1 as it stood through rev 7, word for word.**

> 1. **Land growth.** A 200×200 map at `land_percent 100` is 40k tiles, each one a weighted draw from a frontier of hundreds of candidates. Re-normalizing weights per step is tens of millions of operations before objects are placed. Required: the frontier lives in **fixed integer weight buckets** (Sec.6.1 defines the bucket function), each bucket an append-only `Int32Array` of tile indices with a live count; a draw picks a bucket proportional to `count × weight` then an index within it, both O(1); membership is tracked in a `Uint8Array` so a tile is never enqueued twice, and stale entries are skipped lazily on pop rather than removed. No sorting, no re-weighting, no per-candidate object.
